exam_points: Constructors initialize object states and share the exact name as the class.
Static members belong to the class rather than individual instances.

notes.title: Interfaces, Packages & Exception Handling
notes.explanation: Java supports multiple inheritance via interfaces, modular code grouping via packages, and robust runtime error management using try-catch-finally exception blocks.
definitions: A reference type in Java similar to a class that can contain only constants and abstract method signatures.
A mechanism to handle runtime errors gracefully using try, catch, finally, throw, and throws keywords.
notes.example: try { int x = 5 / 0; } catch(ArithmeticException e) { System.out.println(e); }
exam_points: A class can implement multiple interfaces, achieving multiple inheritance in Java.
The finally block executes unconditionally regardless of whether an exception occurred.

notes.title: Multithreading, Applets & I/O Streams
notes.explanation: Java supports concurrent execution via multithreading (Thread class, Runnable interface) and handles file input/output using byte and character streams.
definitions: Concurrent execution of multiple threads to maximize CPU utilization and application responsiveness.
Java I/O streams (InputStream, OutputStream) used for reading and writing binary raw data.
notes.example: class MyThread extends Thread { public void run() { /* task */ } }
exam_points: Thread lifecycle includes New, Runnable, Blocked, Waiting, and Terminated states.
Thread synchronization prevents race conditions on shared critical resources.

questions: Explain primary features of Java programming language and JVM architecture.
Discuss primitive data types and variable scope rules in Java.
Differentiate between Method Overloading and Method Overriding with examples.
Explain Abstract Classes and Final Classes in Java object-oriented programming.
Explain how Java achieves multiple inheritance using Interfaces.
Discuss Java Exception Handling mechanism with try, catch, finally, and throw blocks.
Explain Thread creation in Java (extending Thread vs implementing Runnable) and thread lifecycle.
Differentiate between Byte Streams and Character Streams in Java I/O.

quiz.question: Which component in Java compiles source code (.java) into bytecode (.class)?
quiz.explanation: javac is the Java compiler tool that generates bytecode files.

quiz.question: Which OOP concept allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method already defined in its superclass?
quiz.explanation: Method overriding provides runtime polymorphism where a subclass redefines a superclass method.

quiz.question: Which keyword is used by a Java class to inherit an interface?
quiz.explanation: Classes use the 'implements' keyword to inherit abstract method contracts from interfaces.

quiz.question: Which block in Java exception handling always executes regardless of exception occurrence?
quiz.explanation: The 'finally' block ensures cleanup code runs unconditionally.

quiz.question: Which interface must a class implement to create a thread by passing it to a Thread object constructor?
quiz.explanation: The Runnable interface defines the run() method for thread execution.

subjects.name: Internet of Things (IoT)
objectives: CO1: Understand IoT architecture, physical/logical designs, and communication protocols.
CO2: Explore domain-specific IoT applications across smart homes, agriculture, and industry.
CO3: Master IoT system management using NETCONF-YANG and Raspberry Pi prototyping.

syllabus.topics: Definition and Need of IoT, Characteristics of IoT, Physical Design of IoT – IoT Protocols, Logical Design of IoT, IoT Enabled Technologies – Wireless Sensor Networks, Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Communication Protocols, Embedded Systems, IoT Levels and Templates.

Domain Specific IoTs – Home, City, Environment, Energy, Retail, Logistics, Agriculture, Industry, Health and Lifestyle. M2M Applications, Software Defined Networks (SDN), Network Function Virtualization (NFV).
Need for IoT System Management, Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), Network Operator Requirements, NETCONF, YANG, IoT System Management with NETCONF-YANG, IoT Design Methodology.

Introduction to Raspberry Pi - Interfaces (serial, SPI, I2C), Introduction to Cloud Storage Models and Communication APIs Webserver – Web Server for IoT, Cloud for IoT, Security Management in an IoT System.

notes.title: IoT Fundamentals & Architecture
notes.explanation: IoT refers to a network of interconnected physical devices embedded with sensors, microcontrollers, software, and communication protocols.
definitions: Wireless Sensor Network: Spatially distributed autonomous sensors monitoring environmental parameters.
Architectural deployment classifications (Level 1 to Level 6) based on local vs cloud compute distribution.
notes.example: Sensors streaming ambient temperature data to cloud analytics engines.
exam_points: IoT physical design covers sensors, actuators, and communication nodes.
Logical design defines functional blocks, communication APIs, and data models.

notes.title: Domain-Specific IoT & SDN/NFV
notes.explanation: IoT transforms vertical domains like smart homes, agriculture, and industrial automation, supported by Software Defined Networks (SDN).
definitions: Software Defined Networking: Network architecture decoupling control plane logic from data forwarding hardware.
Network Function Virtualization: Replacing dedicated network hardware appliances with virtual software instances.
notes.example: Smart agriculture systems utilizing soil moisture sensors to automate drip irrigation.
exam_points: M2M (Machine-to-Machine) communication forms the foundational communication layer for IoT.
Smart cities utilize IoT for traffic management and environmental monitoring.

notes.title: IoT System Management & NETCONF-YANG
notes.explanation: Managing large-scale IoT deployments requires standardized network management protocols like SNMP, NETCONF, and YANG data modeling languages.
definitions: Network Configuration Protocol: XML-based network management protocol operating over secure SSH sessions.
A data modeling language used to describe configuration and state data manipulated by NETCONF.
notes.example: NETCONF-YANG models device configurations hierarchically for automated IoT device management.
exam_points: SNMP manages traditional network devices using MIBs (Management Information Bases).
IoT design methodology outlines requirement specifications, process modeling, and service specifications.

notes.title: Raspberry Pi Prototyping & Cloud Integration
notes.explanation: Raspberry Pi provides a powerful single-board computer platform interfacing with hardware sensors via SPI, I2C, and serial buses, integrated with cloud web servers.
definitions: Inter-Integrated Circuit: A synchronous serial communication protocol using two wires (SDA and SCL).
Serial Peripheral Interface: A synchronous master-slave communication bus supporting high-speed data transfer.
notes.example: Interfacing temperature sensors with Raspberry Pi GPIO pins and streaming data to AWS IoT cloud.
exam_points: Cloud storage models (SaaS, PaaS) store and process high-volume IoT telemetry data.
Security management ensures end-to-end encryption, device authentication, and data integrity.

questions: Define IoT and explain its physical and logical design components.
Discuss IoT levels and templates, comparing them with WSN and Cloud Computing.
Explain domain-specific IoT applications in Smart Agriculture, Smart Cities, and Healthcare.
Differentiate between M2M and IoT, and explain Software Defined Networks (SDN).
Explain the need for IoT system management and compare SNMP with NETCONF-YANG.
Discuss the systematic IoT Design Methodology steps.
Explain Raspberry Pi architecture and serial communication interfaces (SPI, I2C, UART).
Discuss cloud integration, web servers for IoT, and security management challenges.

quiz.question: Which architecture separates network control functionality from physical data forwarding hardware?
quiz.explanation: SDN decouples the control plane from the data forwarding plane.

quiz.question: Which domain-specific IoT application utilizes automated drip irrigation and soil moisture telemetry?
quiz.explanation: Smart agriculture deploys IoT sensors for automated crop watering and soil monitoring.

quiz.question: Which XML-based network configuration protocol operates over SSH for automated device management?
quiz.explanation: NETCONF is designed for network configuration management over secure connections.

quiz.question: Which serial communication protocol uses two wires (SDA and SCL) for synchronous master-slave communication?
quiz.explanation: I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit) uses Serial Data (SDA) and Serial Clock (SCL) lines.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of actuators in an IoT physical system?
options: To convert electrical control signals into physical mechanical movement or action
quiz.explanation: Actuators perform physical actions (like turning on a motor or valve) based on control commands.

subjects.name: Cloud Computing
objectives: CO1: Understand computing paradigms, cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), and deployment models.
CO2: Master virtualization hypervisors, capacity planning, elasticity, and scalability.
CO3: Explore SLA management, cloud security, and industry platforms like AWS and Azure.

syllabus.topics: Overview of Computing Paradigm: Grid Computing, Cluster Computing, Distributed Computing, Utility Computing, Cloud Computing. Introduction to Cloud Computing: Vision, Service Models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), Deployment Models (Public, Private, Hybrid, Community).
Virtualization: Hypervisors (Type-1, Type-2), Taxonomy of Virtualization, Virtualization and Cloud Computing. Capacity Planning: Elasticity vs Scalability, System Metrics, Load Testing.
SLA Management in Cloud Computing, Types of SLA, Life Cycle of SLA. Securing Cloud services: Cloud Security, Encryption, Auditing and compliance.
Cloud Platforms in Industry: Amazon Web Services (EC2, S3), Google AppEngine, Microsoft Azure Core Concepts.

notes.title: Cloud Paradigms & Service Models
notes.explanation: Cloud computing delivers on-demand computing resources over the internet on a pay-as-you-go model, evolving from grid and utility computing.
definitions: Infrastructure as a Service providing virtual compute, storage, and networking resources.
Software as a Service delivering fully functional software applications over the web on demand.
notes.example: AWS EC2 providing dynamic VM compute instances (IaaS); Google Docs (SaaS).
exam_points: Deployment models include Public, Private, Hybrid, and Community clouds.
PaaS provides developer platforms and runtime environments without managing underlying infrastructure.

notes.title: Virtualization & Capacity Planning
notes.explanation: Virtualization abstracts physical hardware using hypervisors, enabling multi-tenancy, elasticity, and dynamic resource scaling in cloud data centers.
definitions: Bare-metal hypervisor running directly on physical server hardware (e.g., VMware ESXi).
The ability of a cloud system to automatically expand or shrink allocated compute resources dynamically based on workload.
notes.example: Type-2 hypervisors like Oracle VirtualBox run on top of an existing host operating system.
exam_points: Scalability handles growing workloads by adding resources vertically (scale-up) or horizontally (scale-out).
Load testing evaluates system performance under peak concurrent user traffic.

notes.title: SLA Management & Cloud Security
notes.explanation: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) legally bind cloud providers to guaranteed uptime and performance metrics, supported by robust encryption and security audits.
definitions: A formal negotiated contract between cloud service provider and consumer defining performance guarantees and penalties.
Policies, technologies, and controls protecting cloud data, applications, and infrastructure from cyber threats.
notes.example: An SLA guaranteeing 99.9% uptime with financial credits issued for SLA breaches.
exam_points: SLA lifecycle encompasses creation, monitoring, enforcement, and termination.
Encryption secures data at rest and data in transit across cloud networks.

notes.title: Industry Cloud Platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP)
notes.explanation: Major cloud providers offer comprehensive enterprise ecosystems, including Amazon Web Services (EC2, S3), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.
definitions: Elastic Compute Cloud: AWS web service providing resizable virtual server instances.
Simple Storage Service: Scalable cloud object storage infrastructure.
notes.example: Deploying web applications on AWS EC2 instances backed by S3 storage buckets.
exam_points: AWS, Azure, and Google App Engine dominate global enterprise cloud deployments.
Cloud storage models offer highly durable, redundant object and block storage.

questions: Compare IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS cloud service delivery models with examples.
Discuss cloud deployment models (Public, Private, Hybrid, Community) and their characteristics.
Explain Virtualization and differentiate between Type-1 (Bare-Metal) and Type-2 (Hosted) hypervisors.
Differentiate between Elasticity and Scalability in cloud computing capacity planning.
Explain SLA management, SLA lifecycle, and penalties for service level violations.
Discuss cloud security measures, data encryption, and compliance auditing.
Explain core services of Amazon Web Services (AWS) such as EC2 and S3.
Compare Microsoft Azure and Google App Engine core cloud platform architectures.

quiz.question: Which cloud service model provides raw virtualized hardware, storage, and networking infrastructure to users?
quiz.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) delivers foundational virtual compute and storage resources.

quiz.question: Which type of hypervisor runs directly on bare-metal server hardware without requiring an underlying host operating system?
quiz.explanation: Type-1 hypervisors execute directly on physical server hardware for maximum performance.

quiz.question: What term describes a cloud system's automatic capability to expand or reduce compute resource allocations dynamically based on workload?
quiz.explanation: Elasticity automatically matches resource provisioning to fluctuating workload demands.

quiz.question: What does SLA stand for in cloud computing contracts?
quiz.explanation: SLA stands for Service Level Agreement, defining uptime guarantees and performance metrics.

quiz.question: Which AWS core service provides scalable object storage for files and data backups?
quiz.explanation: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is the industry-standard cloud object storage service.

subjects.name: Minor Project
objectives: CO1: Identify real-world problem statements and formulate comprehensive SRS specifications.
CO2: Design system architecture, database schemas, and full-stack software components.
CO3: Implement, test, and document production-ready software solutions with viva-voce presentation.

syllabus.topics: Problem Statement Identification, SRS Formulation, System Design Architecture, Full-Stack Implementation, Documentation & Viva-Voce.

notes.title: Problem Statement & SRS Documentation
notes.explanation: Minor project execution begins with identifying a meaningful software problem statement, conducting feasibility studies, and documenting functional and non-functional requirements in an SRS.
definitions: A concise description of an issue or pain point that needs to be addressed through a software solution.
Software Requirements Specification: A formal document outlining functional requirements, user actors, and system constraints.
notes.example: Developing an AI-powered college help desk chatbot or an interactive RAG knowledge base.
exam_points: Feasibility analysis evaluates technical, economic, and operational viability.
SRS acts as the foundational blueprint guiding development and testing phases.

notes.title: System Design, Implementation & Testing
notes.explanation: System architecture design involves creating database schemas, UML diagrams, and API endpoints, followed by iterative full-stack coding and rigorous testing.
definitions: The conceptual model defining structure, behavior, and views of a software system.
Building both client-side user interfaces and server-side backend logic connected to persistent databases.
notes.example: Building web applications using Python (FastAPI/Flask) backend, HTML/CSS/JS frontend, and SQLite/ChromaDB databases.
exam_points: Version control using Git and GitHub ensures collaborative code management.
Project finalization requires comprehensive documentation, live deployment, and faculty viva-voce presentation.

questions: Explain the steps involved in identifying a software problem statement and formulating an SRS document.
Discuss system architecture design, database schema modeling, and full-stack integration strategies for your minor project.
Explain software testing methodologies and documentation standards required for project viva-voce evaluation.

subjects.name: Mentorship & Professional Development (MPD)
objectives: CO1: Enhance soft skills, professional communication, and business etiquette.
CO2: Master resume building, LinkedIn branding, and technical interview preparation.
CO3: Practice quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, and placement assessment tests.

syllabus.topics: Soft Skills Enhancement, Resume Building, Interview Etiquette, Quantitative Aptitude & Placement Preparation.

notes.title: Soft Skills & Professional Communication
notes.explanation: Professional development emphasizes effective verbal and written communication, active listening, teamwork, and corporate workplace etiquette.
definitions: Personal attributes and interpersonal communication abilities that enable effective interaction with others.
Standard codes of professional conduct and polite behavior expected in workplace environments.
notes.example: Demonstrating active listening and constructive feedback during team collaboration meetings.
exam_points: Clear professional communication prevents misunderstandings in technical team projects.
Body language and professional demeanor are vital during corporate interactions.

notes.title: Resume Building & Interview Preparation
notes.explanation: Crafting a professional ATS-friendly resume and mastering technical/HR interview etiquette are crucial steps for successful campus placements.
definitions: Applicant Tracking System compatible resume optimized with clear headings and relevant keyword phrasing.
Interview response structure: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
notes.example: Structuring project achievements on LinkedIn and resume using quantifiable metrics.
exam_points: Resumes should highlight technical stack proficiencies, internships, and capstone projects.
Mock interviews build confidence and refine technical communication skills.

notes.title: Quantitative Aptitude & Logical Reasoning
notes.explanation: Campus placement tests assess analytical thinking through quantitative aptitude, data interpretation, and logical reasoning problem-solving.
definitions: Mathematical problem-solving ability covering arithmetic, algebra, number systems, and data interpretation.
Analytical problem-solving testing pattern recognition, puzzles, syllogisms, and deductive reasoning.
notes.example: Solving percentage, time-speed-distance, and data interpretation charts efficiently under timed conditions.
exam_points: Regular practice of aptitude shortcuts improves placement test scores.
Coding aptitude rounds test data structures and algorithms problem-solving proficiency.

questions: Discuss the importance of soft skills and professional communication in corporate careers.
Explain how to structure an ATS-friendly resume and prepare for technical and HR interviews using the STAR method.
Discuss key quantitative aptitude and logical reasoning strategies for campus placement examinations.

quiz.question: What term refers to personal attributes, communication abilities, and interpersonal skills in a workplace?
quiz.explanation: Soft skills encompass communication, teamwork, and emotional intelligence.

quiz.question: What does ATS stand for in modern resume evaluation and recruiting?
quiz.explanation: ATS stands for Applicant Tracking System, used by recruiters to filter resumes.

quiz.question: What does the acronym STAR stand for in behavioral interview question responses?
quiz.explanation: STAR framework structures behavioral answers by detailing Situation, Task, Action, and Result.

quiz.question: Which area of placement preparation evaluates analytical problem-solving, arithmetic, and data interpretation?
quiz.explanation: Quantitative aptitude tests mathematical and analytical problem-solving skills.

subjects.name: Android Programming
objectives: CO1: Prepare environment for working on Android OS.
CO2: Highlight various security issues in Android platform.
CO3: Design innovative User Interface and develop activity for android app.
CO4: Outline the steps for creating database applications.
CO5: Write programs for basic Android based applications.

syllabus.topics: Characteristics of Mobile applications, Introduction to Android Development Environment, Advantages and Features of Android, Architecture and working of Android, User-interface design for mobile applications and managing application data.
Integrating cloud services, networking, OS and hardware into mobile applications. Enterprise requirements in mobile applications: Performance, Scalability, Modifiability, Availability and Security.
Mobile Software Engineering (Design Principles, Development, Testing methodologies for mobile applications).
Directory Structure of an Android Project, Common Default Resources Folders, The Values Folder, Leveraging Android XML.

notes.title: Android Architecture & UI Basics
notes.explanation: Android is a Linux-based open-source mobile OS composed of Linux Kernel, HAL, Native Libraries, Android Runtime (ART/Dalvik), Application Framework, and Applications.
definitions: A single visual screen representing a user interface component in an Android application.
An asynchronous messaging object used to request an action from another app component.
notes.example: setContentView(R.layout.activity_main); sets the layout view for an Activity.
exam_points: Four core application components: Activities, Services, Broadcast Receivers, Content Providers.
Android Runtime (ART) uses Ahead-Of-Time (AOT) compilation to improve execution efficiency.

notes.title: Enterprise Requirements, Cloud Services & Security
notes.explanation: Enterprise mobile applications require robust performance, scalability, security, availability, and cloud web service integrations.
definitions: An isolation mechanism executed via Linux user IDs ensuring each app runs in its own process without unauthorized data access.
Architectural style for mobile-to-cloud network communication using HTTP requests and JSON responses.
notes.example: Requesting user runtime permissions dynamically for sensitive hardware access like Camera or GPS.
exam_points: Security vulnerabilities stem from insecure data storage, weak transport layer encryption, and over-privileged permissions.
Modifiability and scalability are achieved by separating presentation, business logic, and networking layers.

notes.title: Mobile Software Engineering & Testing
notes.explanation: Mobile software engineering emphasizes agile development methodologies, responsive UI design principles, resource optimization, and automated testing.
definitions: Testing individual methods and components using JUnit and Mockito frameworks.
UI tests running directly on physical devices or emulators using frameworks like Espresso.
notes.example: Testing app behavior under low memory, screen rotation, and varying network conditions.
exam_points: Mobile lifecycle management handles configuration changes (e.g., orientation) cleanly without losing state.
Design principles focus on battery life management, touch targets, and offline-first data caching.

notes.title: Android Project Directory Structure & XML Resources
notes.explanation: An Android project follows a standardized directory structure separating Java/Kotlin source files, manifest declarations, and XML layout/value resources.
definitions: The essential control file declaring app components, hardware requirements, and system permissions.
Directory containing XML resource files for strings.xml, colors.xml, styles.xml, and dimens.xml.
notes.example: <TextView android:layout_width="wrap_content" android:layout_height="wrap_content" android:text="@string/app_name" />
exam_points: res/layout stores UI XML layouts; res/drawable stores graphics and shape selectors.
Leveraging XML allows decoupling user interface layout design from backend Java logic.

questions: Explain the layer-by-layer architecture of the Android Operating System with a clean diagram.
What are the four primary application components in Android? Explain each briefly.
Discuss enterprise non-functional requirements (Performance, Scalability, Security, Availability) in mobile app development.
Explain how Android handles security, application sandboxing, and runtime permission models.
Explain mobile software engineering design principles and testing methodologies (Unit Testing vs UI Instrumentation Testing).
Discuss the Activity Lifecycle states and callback methods executed during configuration changes.
Detail the directory structure of a standard Android project, explaining the significance of java, res, and manifest folders.
How are XML layouts and value resources (strings.xml, colors.xml, styles.xml) leveraged in Android UI design?

quiz.question: Which layer of the Android architecture acts as an abstraction between physical device hardware and the software stack?
quiz.explanation: HAL provides standard interfaces exposing physical hardware capabilities to higher-level Java frameworks.

quiz.question: How does the Android OS isolate individual installed applications from accessing each other's data illegally?
options: By assigning a unique Linux User ID (UID) and sandboxing process execution
By locking the database with standard passwords
quiz.explanation: Each Android app runs in a separate process with its own unique Linux UID sandbox.

quiz.question: Which Android UI automated testing framework is commonly used for instrumentation testing on real devices?
quiz.explanation: Espresso provides APIs for writing reliable user interface tests within Android applications.

quiz.question: Which XML file serves as the root manifest file declaring all activities, permissions, and services?
quiz.explanation: AndroidManifest.xml declares essential system-level information and application component registrations.

quiz.question: Inside which res subfolder are XML layout resource files stored?
quiz.explanation: All XML layout files defining user interfaces are stored in the res/layout folder.

subjects.name: Artificial Intelligence
objectives: CO1: Highlight the significance and domains of Artificial Intelligence and knowledge representation.
CO2: Outline the advantages and disadvantages of various search techniques.
CO3: Identify various Expert Systems and AI applications.
CO4: Define the role of AI in different areas like NLP, Pattern Recognition etc.
CO5: Select the right AI tool for different AI based applications.

syllabus.topics: Introduction-What is intelligence? Foundations of artificial intelligence (AI). History of AI. AI problems: Toy Problems, Real World problems- Tic-Tac-Toe, Water Jug, Question-Answering, 8-puzzle, 8-Queens problem. Formulating problems, Searching for Solutions. Knowledge Representation: Propositional Logic, Propositional Theorem Proving-Inference and Proofs, Proof by Resolution, Horn Clauses and definite Clauses, Forward and Backward chaining; First order Logic, Inference in First Order Logic.

Uncertain Knowledge and Reasoning: Basic probability, Bayes rule, Belief networks, Default reasoning, Fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic. Structured Knowledge: Associative Networks, Frame Structures, Conceptual Dependencies and Scripts.

Uninformed Search strategies- Breadth-first search, Uniform-cost search, Depth-first search, Depth-limited search, Iterative deepening depth-first search, Bidirectional search, Comparing uninformed search strategies. Informed (Heuristic) Search Strategies- Hill Climbing, Simulated Annealing, Genetic Algorithm, Greedy best-first search, A* and optimal search, Memory-bounded heuristic search.

Natural language processing: Grammars, Parsing. Pattern Recognition: Recognition and Classification Process-Decision Theoretic Classification, Syntactic Classification; Learning Classification Patterns, Recognizing and Understanding Speech. Expert System Architectures: Characteristics, Rule-Based System Architectures, Nonproduction System Architectures, Knowledge Acquisition and Validation.

notes.title: AI Problems & Knowledge Representation
notes.explanation: Artificial Intelligence formulates problems as state-space searches (e.g., 8-Puzzle, Water Jug) and represents knowledge using Propositional and First-Order Logic.
definitions: An inference rule in formal logic that derives contradictions from negated goal statements to prove theorem validity.
A clause containing at most one positive literal, enabling efficient forward and backward chaining inference.
notes.example: Solving the 8-Queens problem by placing queens on an 8x8 grid without mutual attacks.
exam_points: Forward chaining is data-driven; backward chaining is goal-driven.
First-Order Logic adds predicates, functions, and quantifiers (Universal \forall, Existential \exists) to Propositional Logic.

notes.title: Reasoning Under Uncertainty & Structured Knowledge
notes.explanation: Uncertain knowledge is modeled using Bayes' Rule, Belief Networks, and Fuzzy Logic, while structured knowledge uses Semantic Networks, Frames, and Scripts.
definitions: A directed acyclic graph representing random variables and their conditional dependencies.
A mathematical logic handling truth values ranging continuously between 0.0 (false) and 1.0 (true).
notes.example: Frames use slot-and-filler structures to represent structured object domain knowledge.
exam_points: Bayes' rule updates probability estimates upon receiving new evidence.
Conceptual Dependency (CD) represents natural language sentences using primitive action structures.

notes.title: Uninformed & Informed (Heuristic) Search
notes.explanation: State-space search strategies explore problem graphs using uninformed brute-force or informed heuristic functions ($f(n) = g(n) + h(n)$).
definitions: An optimal heuristic search algorithm combining actual path cost $g(n)$ and estimated cost to goal $h(n)$.
A heuristic $h(n)$ that never overestimates the actual minimal cost to reach the goal state.
notes.example: BFS uses a Queue data structure; DFS uses a Stack data structure.
exam_points: Iterative Deepening combines space efficiency of DFS with completeness of BFS.
Simulated Annealing avoids local maxima in Hill Climbing by allowing random downhill moves early.

notes.title: NLP, Pattern Recognition & Expert Systems
notes.explanation: AI applications encompass Natural Language Processing (parsing, grammars), Pattern Recognition (speech, syntactic classification), and Rule-Based Expert Systems.
definitions: A computer program using a knowledge base and inference engine to solve complex domain problems like a human expert.
Analyzing a sequence of natural language tokens to determine its grammatical structure relative to a formal grammar.
notes.example: MYCIN expert system for medical diagnosis using IF-THEN rule production architectures.
exam_points: Pattern recognition uses decision-theoretic or syntactic classification methods.
Knowledge acquisition extracts domain expertise from human experts for system validation.

questions: Formulate the Water Jug Problem and 8-Puzzle Problem using state-space representation.
Explain Proof by Resolution in First-Order Logic with a complete example derivation.
Explain Bayes' Rule and how Bayesian Belief Networks model reasoning under uncertainty.
Discuss Structured Knowledge representation techniques: Semantic Networks, Frames, and Scripts.
Compare Uninformed search strategies: BFS, DFS, UCS, and Iterative Deepening DFS in terms of time, space, completeness, and optimality.
Explain A* Search algorithm, state its admissibility condition, and prove its optimality.
Explain the architecture of a Rule-Based Expert System detailing the Inference Engine and Knowledge Base.
Discuss Natural Language Processing parsing phases and Pattern Recognition classification models.

quiz.question: Which inference mechanism starts from known facts and applies rules iteratively to derive new conclusions in a data-driven manner?
quiz.explanation: Forward chaining is a data-driven approach executing rules whose premises match current known facts.

quiz.question: Which structured knowledge representation format uses slot and filler properties to represent objects and concepts?
quiz.explanation: Frames store domain knowledge about objects using structured attributes (slots) and values (fillers).

quiz.question: What property must a heuristic function h(n) satisfy to guarantee that A* search finds the optimal path?
quiz.explanation: Admissibility requires $h(n)$ to never overestimate the actual remaining path cost to the goal.

quiz.question: Which search algorithm uses a memory-efficient strategy by iteratively executing Depth-Limited Search with increasing depth limits?
quiz.explanation: Iterative Deepening DFS combines the linear memory advantage of DFS with the completeness of BFS.

quiz.question: Which key component of an Expert System executes rules from the Knowledge Base to answer queries?
quiz.explanation: The Inference Engine processes facts and rules from the knowledge base to derive conclusions.

subjects.name: R Programming
objectives: CO1: Identify the key components of R programming Language.
CO2: Define the concept of data Science.
CO3: Differentiate between vectors and arrays.
CO4: Outline the usage of data frames, lists, factors, tables and R structures.
CO5: Explain the need and utilization of various visualization tools.

syllabus.topics: R Programming Fundamentals: Introduction to R, Installing R, Windows/Linux/Mac Installation, Setting up Path, Using Packages, and Running R: Interactive Mode, Batch Mode, Getting Help, Startup and Shut Down. Vectors: Scalars, Vectors, Arrays and Matrices, Declarations, Recycling, Common Vector Operations, Using all() and any(), Na and Null Values, Filtering, ifelse() Function. Matrices and Arrays: Creating Matrices, General Matrix Operations, Applying Functions to Matrix Rows and Columns, Adding & Deleting Matrix Rows and Columns, Difference Between Matrix and Vector.

Lists: Creating Lists, General List Operations, Accessing List Components and Values, Applying Functions to Lists, Recursive Lists. Data Frames: Creating Data Frames, Merging Data Frames, Applying Functions to Data Frames. Factors and Tables: Introduction, Common Functions use with Factors, Working with Tables. R Programming Structures: Control Statements, Arithmetic and Boolean Operators, Default Values for Arguments, Return Values, Recursion.

Object Oriented Programming: Concept of Classes, S3 Classes, S4 Classes, S3 Versus S4 Classes, Managing Objects. Input/Output: Accessing Keyboard and Monitor, Reading and Writing Files, Accessing the Internet. String Manipulation: Overview of String Manipulation Functions [grep(), nchar(), paste(), sprintf(), substr(), strsplit(), regexpr(), gregexpr(), Regular expression].

Graphics: Creating Graphs, Customizing Graphs, Saving Graphs to Files, Creating 3D Plots. Debugging: Principles of Debugging, Use of Debugging Tool, Using R Programming Debugging Facilities. Simulation: Generating Random Numbers, Setting the Random Number Seed, Simulating a Linear Model, Random Sampling.

notes.title: R Fundamentals, Vectors, Matrices & Arrays
notes.explanation: R is an open-source programming environment optimized for statistical analysis, data science, matrix computations, and data visualization.
definitions: Automatic repetition of elements of a shorter vector when performing operations with a longer vector.
A two-dimensional homogenous data structure containing elements of the same primitive data type.
notes.example: apply(matrix_data, 1, sum) calculates row-wise sums in R.
exam_points: R vectors are 1-indexed (indices start at 1, not 0).
Difference: Vectors are 1D homogenous; Matrices are 2D homogenous; Data Frames are 2D heterogenous.

notes.title: Lists, Data Frames, Factors & Control Structures
notes.explanation: R manages heterogenous datasets via Lists and Data Frames, categorical data via Factors, and control logic via loops and functions.
definitions: A 2D tabular data structure where different columns can store different data types (heterogenous).
A data object used to store and manage categorical variables with predefined level categories.
notes.example: df <- data.frame(Name=c('Alice','Bob'), Age=c(20, 22)); creates a Data Frame.
exam_points: lapply() applies a function over a list and returns a list; sapply() simplifies results into a vector.
Functions support default argument values and recursive invocation.

notes.title: OOP (S3 vs S4), File I/O & String Functions
notes.explanation: R implements Object-Oriented Programming using informal S3 and formal S4 classes, alongside robust file I/O and regular expression string functions.
definitions: Informal, lightweight OOP class system in R relying on generic functions and attributes.
Formal, strict OOP class system in R defined using setClass() with explicit slot type declarations.
notes.example: paste('Hello', 'World', sep=' ') concatenates strings together.
exam_points: Functions like grep(), substr(), strsplit(), and sprintf() manipulate strings and regular expressions.
read.csv() and write.csv() handle file I/O operations.

notes.title: Graphics, Debugging & Statistical Simulation
notes.explanation: R provides built-in graphical plotting facilities (plot, hist), debugging tools (browser, trace), and statistical simulation functions.
definitions: A function used to set the random number generator seed, ensuring reproducible simulation results.
An interactive debugging facility in R that pauses function execution and allows step-by-step inspection.
notes.example: rnorm(100, mean=0, sd=1) generates 100 random numbers from a standard normal distribution.
exam_points: Graphs can be customized with main titles, axis labels, colors, and saved to PDF or PNG devices.
Random sampling is executed using the sample() function with or without replacement.

questions: Explain Vector Recycling rule in R with code illustrations.
Differentiate between Vectors, Matrices, and Multi-dimensional Arrays in R.
Differentiate between Lists and Data Frames in R, demonstrating how to access components of each.
Explain Factors in R and discuss common functions used for categorical table processing.
Compare S3 and S4 Object Oriented Programming class systems in R with code examples.
Explain key string manipulation functions in R: grep(), paste(), substr(), and strsplit().
Discuss R graphics facilities for customizing and saving 2D and 3D plots.
Explain statistical simulation functions (rnorm, sample, set.seed) and R debugging facilities.

quiz.question: What is the starting index of vectors and arrays in R programming?
quiz.explanation: Unlike C/Java (0-indexed), R vectors and arrays are 1-indexed.

quiz.question: Which data structure in R allows columns to hold different data types (e.g., numeric, character, boolean) simultaneously?
quiz.explanation: Data Frames are 2D heterogenous tabular structures capable of holding multiple data types across columns.

quiz.question: Which R string manipulation function splits a string vector into substrings based on a delimiter?
quiz.explanation: strsplit() splits character strings into sub-tokens using specified regex delimiters.

quiz.question: Which function defines a formal S4 class structure with explicit slot types in R?
quiz.explanation: S4 classes are explicitly declared using the setClass() constructor function.

quiz.question: Which function sets the random number generator state to ensure reproducible statistical simulations in R?
quiz.explanation: set.seed() initializes the pseudo-random number generator for reproducible sampling.

subjects.name: Digital Marketing
objectives: CO1: Highlight the key elements of a digital marketing strategy.
CO2: Choose the right platform for digital marketing.
CO3: Identify the major digital marketing channels.
CO4: Design content for digital marketing.
CO5: Develop digital marketing strategy and plan.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Digital Marketing: Difference between Traditional Marketing and Digital Marketing, Benefits of using Digital Media, Inbound and Outbound Marketing, Online marketing POEM: (Paid, Owned, and Earned Media), Components of Online Marketing (Email, Forum, Social network, Banner, Blog), Impact of Online Marketing, Basics of Affiliate Marketing, Viral Marketing, Influencer Marketing, Referral Marketing. Email Marketing: Email newsletters, Digests, Dedicated Emails, Lead Nurturing, Sponsorship Emails and Transactional Emails, Drawbacks of Email Marketing. Social Media Marketing (SMM): Different types of Social Media Marketing like Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, Video, Instagram etc.

Search Engine Optimisation (SEO): About SEO, Need of an SEO friendly website, Importance of Internet and Search Engines; Role of Keywords in SEO. On-Page Optimization (Onsite): Basics of Website Designing / Development; HTML Basics for SEO; Onsite Optimization Basics; Website Structure and Navigation Menu Optimization; SEO Content Writing. Keywords Research and Analysis (eg. SWOT analysis of website, finding appropriate keywords). Off Page Optimization: Introduction; Local marketing of websites depending on locations; Promoting Subsequent pages of the website. Introduction to organic SEO vs non-organic SEO; Social Media Optimization Techniques and Page Rank Technology.

Website Planning & Creation: Content Marketing Strategy: Goals and concepts, Strategic building blocks, Content creation & channel distribution, Tools of the trade, Advantages and challenges. Keywords Research and Analysis: Introduction to Keyword Research; Business Analysis; Types of Keywords; Keywords Analysis Tools. Web Presence: How to increase online presence and drive more traffic for a website, Search result visibility in search engines for chosen keyword and phrases, Using e-mail marketing to drive traffic for a website, Posting social media content for lead generation, Tools to create and manage content, Use of Blogging as content strategy. Creating content: Writing and posting content on the web and in social networks, blog and video; Create, manage and implement a content marketing strategy; Monitoring and recording results to improve content marketing campaigns; Successful content marketing strategies and case studies.

Online Advertising, Mobile Marketing and Web analytics: Introduction to Online Advertising and its advantages, Paid versus Organic, Pay Per Click (PPC) Model. Basic concepts Cost per Click (CPC), CPM, CTR, CR etc. About Mobile Marketing, Objectives of Mobile Advertising, Creating a Mobile Marketing Strategy, Introduction to SMS Marketing. About Web Analytics, Types of Web Analytics (On-site, Off-site), Importance of Web Analytics.

notes.title: Digital Marketing Foundations, POEM & SMM
notes.explanation: Digital marketing leverages digital channels, social platforms, email, and media channels to reach consumers targetably and measurably.
definitions: Paid Media (sponsored ads), Owned Media (brand website/social pages), and Earned Media (viral word-of-mouth/shares).
Attracting customers by creating valuable content and tailored experiences rather than intrusive ads.
notes.example: Promoting products using Instagram Reels, LinkedIn posts, and transactional email newsletters.
exam_points: Email marketing formats include newsletters, lead nurturing drips, and transactional receipts.
Affiliate marketing rewards third-party publishers for driving traffic or sales.

notes.title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO: On-Page & Off-Page)
notes.explanation: SEO improves organic website visibility on search engine result pages (SERPs) through technical optimization and quality backlinks.
definitions: Optimizing website elements like HTML title tags, meta descriptions, headings, content, and site architecture.
Activities conducted outside the website, such as backlink building, local listings, and social signals.
notes.example: Conducting keyword research using Google Keyword Planner for SWOT content optimization.
exam_points: Organic SEO builds free long-term traffic; non-organic (PPC) requires paid ad budgets.
Google PageRank evaluates backlink quantity and quality to rank web pages.

notes.title: Content Strategy, Keyword Research & Web Presence
notes.explanation: Planning web presence requires aligning keyword research, content creation, social media distributions, and analytics monitoring.
definitions: Identifying search terms and phrases that target audiences enter into search engines.
Creating and distributing valuable, relevant content to attract and retain a clearly defined audience.
notes.example: Publishing weekly authoritative blog posts optimized for long-tail keywords.
exam_points: Blogging drives domain authority, search indexation, and social lead generation.
Monitoring metrics ensures content campaigns are optimized over time.

notes.title: Online Advertising, Mobile Marketing & Web Analytics
notes.explanation: Digital advertising relies on performance models (PPC, CPC, CPM), mobile strategies (SMS, in-app ads), and web analytics tracking.
definitions: The percentage of people who clicked an ad out of total impressions ($CTR = \frac{\text{Clicks}}{\text{Impressions}} \times 100$).
Measuring, collecting, analyzing, and reporting web data to optimize website usage and ROI.
notes.example: Running Pay-Per-Click (PPC) campaigns on Google Ads targeting specific search intents.
exam_points: CPC = Cost Per Click; CPM = Cost Per Thousand Impressions; CR = Conversion Rate.
On-site analytics measures user behavior on-page; off-site analytics measures total market reach.

questions: Differentiate between Traditional Marketing and Digital Marketing. Explain the POEM framework.
Explain Social Media Marketing (SMM) strategies across Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, and Instagram.
Explain Search Engine Optimization (SEO), detailing On-Page and Off-Page optimization techniques.
Compare Organic SEO with Non-Organic (Paid) SEO and explain PageRank technology.
Discuss Content Marketing Strategy building blocks, channel distribution, and keyword analysis tools.
How can blogging and social media content strategies be leveraged to build online web presence?
Explain Online Advertising payment models: Pay-Per-Click (PPC), CPC, CPM, CTR, and Conversion Rate (CR).
Discuss Mobile Marketing strategies (SMS, In-App) and On-site vs Off-site Web Analytics.

quiz.question: In the POEM digital marketing framework, what does the letter 'E' stand for?
quiz.explanation: POEM stands for Paid, Owned, and Earned Media.

quiz.question: Which of the following activities is considered an On-Page SEO optimization technique?
options: Optimizing HTML title tags and meta descriptions
quiz.explanation: Optimizing HTML title tags, headings, and internal content is core to On-Page SEO.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of conducting Keyword Research in digital content planning?
options: To identify real search terms used by target audiences on search engines
quiz.explanation: Keyword research uncovers search intent and terms entered by prospective customers.

quiz.question: Which advertising performance metric measures the percentage of ad impressions that resulted in a user click?
quiz.explanation: CTR measures total ad clicks divided by total ad impressions multiplied by 100.

quiz.question: Which advertising model charges the advertiser only when a user actually clicks on their digital ad link?
quiz.explanation: PPC/CPC billing charges advertisers solely when an user clicks the ad link.

subjects.name: Information Security
objectives: CO1: Identify issues involved in the field of information security.
CO2: Categorize various types of viruses.
CO3: Outline the information security risks across the Internet and WWW.
CO4: Explain different encryption techniques.
CO5: Define cryptography.

syllabus.topics: The Security Problem in Computing: The meaning of computer Security, Computer Criminals, Methods of Defense, Elementary Cryptography: Substitution Ciphers, Transpositions, Making Good Encryption algorithms, Secure Architecture of an open System. DES and RSA Algorithm, Asymmetric and symmetric Key Cryptography, Role based Security, Digital Signatures, The Data Encryption Standard, The AES Encryption Algorithms, Public Key Encryptions, Uses of Encryption.

Security in Program and Operating System: Secure Programs, Non malicious Program Errors, viruses and other malicious code, Targeted Malicious code, controls Against Program Threats, Protection in General- Purpose operating system protected objects and methods of protection memory and addmens protection, File protection Mechanisms, User Authentication Designing Trusted Operating System: Security polices, models of security, trusted Operating System design, Assurance in trusted Operating System Implementation examples.

Database and Network Security: Database Integration and Secrecy, Inferential Control, Sensitive data, Inference, multilevel database, proposals for multilevel security. Security in Network: Threats in Network, Network Security Controls, Firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems, Secure E-Mail.

Administering Security: Security Planning, Risk Analysis, Organizational Security policies, Physical Security. Legal Privacy and Ethical Issues in Computer Security: Protecting Programs and data, Information and the law, Rights of Employees and Employers, Software failures, Computer Crime, Privacy, Ethical issues in Computer Security, Case Studies of Corporate Security.

notes.title: Cryptography (Symmetric, Asymmetric, DES, AES, RSA)
notes.explanation: Cryptography protects information by transforming plaintext into unreadable ciphertext using symmetric (secret key) or asymmetric (public-private key pair) algorithms.
definitions: Encryption scheme using the exact same shared secret key for both encryption and decryption (e.g., DES, AES).
Encryption scheme using a mathematically linked Public Key for encryption and Private Key for decryption (e.g., RSA).
notes.example: Digital Signatures use a sender's Private Key to sign data, verifying authenticity and non-repudiation.
exam_points: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) supports 128, 192, and 256-bit key lengths.
RSA security relies on the computational difficulty of factoring large composite prime numbers.

notes.title: Program & Operating System Security
notes.explanation: OS and program security prevents malicious code (viruses, worms, trojans), buffer overflows, unauthorized memory access, and enforces trusted user authentication.
definitions: Malicious code that attaches itself to host executable files and replicates when the host executes.
A vulnerability occurring when data written to a memory buffer exceeds limits, overwriting adjacent memory space.
notes.example: File permission access control lists (ACLs) governing user read, write, and execute rights.
exam_points: Worms self-replicate independently over network connections without requiring a host executable.
Trusted Operating Systems implement formal security policies (e.g., Bell-LaPadula model).

notes.title: Database & Network Security
notes.explanation: Network and database security protects multi-level databases from inference attacks and network channels from intrusion using Firewalls and IDS.
definitions: A network security system inspecting incoming/outgoing traffic based on predefined security rules.
A device or software application monitoring network traffic for malicious activity or policy violations.
notes.example: Secure E-Mail protocols like S/MIME or PGP providing end-to-end message encryption.
exam_points: Inference control prevents unauthorized users from deducing confidential statistical data.
Firewalls operate as Packet Filters, Stateful Inspection, or Application Gateways.

notes.title: Security Administration, Risk Analysis & Ethics
notes.explanation: Administering security involves organizational risk analysis, physical security controls, privacy law compliance, and resolving corporate ethical issues.
definitions: Assessing assets, vulnerabilities, threats, and potential financial impact to implement cost-effective controls.
Assurance that the sender of data cannot deny having sent the message.
notes.example: Enforcing physical access controls such as biometric scanners at data center entrances.
exam_points: Organizational security policies establish acceptable use and data governance guidelines.
Legal protection includes intellectual property laws, patents, copyrights, and computer crime statutes.

questions: Compare Symmetric Key Cryptography and Asymmetric Key Cryptography with examples.
Explain DES (Data Encryption Standard) and RSA public key encryption algorithms.
Differentiate between Viruses, Worms, Trojan Horses, and Targeted Malicious Code.
Explain file protection mechanisms, memory protection, and Trusted Operating System design models.
Explain Database Security challenges, Multilevel Databases, and Inferential Controls.
Discuss Network Security controls: Firewalls (types), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and Secure E-Mail.
Explain Security Planning and Risk Analysis methodologies in computer security administration.
Discuss legal, ethical, and privacy issues in computer security, including software failures and employee rights.

quiz.question: Which cryptographic algorithm relies on the mathematical difficulty of factoring large prime numbers for key generation?
quiz.explanation: RSA asymmetric public-key cryptography derives security from prime factorization difficulty.

quiz.question: Which type of malicious software self-replicates independently over networks without needing to attach to a host program file?
quiz.explanation: Worms spread autonomously over network connections without requiring user execution or host files.

quiz.question: Which network security device monitors network traffic and alerts administrators upon detecting suspicious signature activity?
quiz.explanation: IDS actively inspects network traffic streams for malicious attack signatures.

quiz.question: In asymmetric cryptography, which key does a sender use to create a Digital Signature verifying message authenticity?
quiz.explanation: Digital signatures are created using the sender's Private Key and verified using their Public Key.

quiz.question: What security term describes preventing a sender from falsely denying that they originated a specific transaction?
quiz.explanation: Non-repudiation ensures cryptographic proof of transaction authorship that cannot be disputed.

subjects.name: Cyber Laws & IPR
objectives: CO1: Identify statutory, regulatory, constitutional, and organizational laws that affect the information technology professional.
CO2: Categorize case law and common law to current legal dilemmas in the technology field.
CO3: Outline the primary forms of intellectual property rights.
CO4: Compare the different forms of intellectual property protection in terms of their key differences and similarities.
CO5: Analyze the effects of intellectual property rights on society as a whole.

syllabus.topics: Overview of Computer and Web Technology, Need for Cyber Law, Cyber Jurisprudence at International and Indian Level, Jurisdictional Aspects in Cyber Law, Issues of jurisdiction in cyberspace, Types of jurisdiction, Minimum Contacts Theory, Sliding Scale Theory, Effects Test and International targeting, Jurisdiction under IT Act, 2000.

Cyber Crimes against Individuals, Institution and State, Hacking, Digital Forgery, Cyber Stalking/Harassment, Ethics and Etiquettes of Cyber World, Cyber Pornography, Identity Theft & Fraud, Cyber Terrorism, Cyber Defamation, Right to Privacy and Data Protection on Internet, Concept of privacy, Threat to privacy on internet, Self-regulation approach to privacy.

Introduction and the need for intellectual property right (IPR), IPR in India – Genesis and Development, IPR in abroad, Data Protection, Open Source Software, Macro economic impact of the patent system, Patent and kind of inventions protected by a patent, Patent document How to protect your inventions?, Granting of patent, Rights of a patent.

What is copyright? Latest editions of Designs, what is covered by copyright? How long does copyright last? Why protect copyright? What are related rights?, Distinction between related rights and copyright?, What is a trademark? Rights of trademark?, What kind of signs can be used as trademarks?, types of trademark, function does a trademark perform, How is a trademark protected?, How is a trademark registered?

notes.title: Cyber Jurisprudence & Jurisdiction
notes.explanation: Cyber law deals with legal issues related to the use of networked information technology. Due to the borderless nature of cyberspace, jurisdictional theories such as Minimum Contacts Theory and Zippo Sliding Scale Theory determine territorial jurisdiction.
definitions: A legal doctrine establishing that a court has jurisdiction over a non-resident defendant if they have sufficient minimum contacts with the forum state.
Framework from Zippo Manufacturing Co. case categorizing websites into passive, interactive, or commercial to determine jurisdiction.
notes.example: Section 75 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 applies to offenses committed outside India if the act involves a computer system located in India.
exam_points: IT Act, 2000 provides extraterritorial jurisdiction under Section 75.
Zippo case established the sliding scale test for internet jurisdiction.

notes.title: Cyber Crimes & Data Privacy
notes.explanation: Cybercrimes target or use computers, networks, or digital devices. Key threats include identity theft, hacking, harassment, and privacy violations.
definitions: Unauthorized access to or alteration of computer systems or networks.
The legal right of individuals to control the collection, storage, and processing of their personal data.
notes.example: Phishing emails crafted to capture user credentials fall under digital fraud and identity theft under IT Act Section 66D.
exam_points: Section 66 defines hacking and computerized fraud punishments.
Self-regulation and statutory frameworks protect privacy online.

notes.title: Overview of Intellectual Property Rights & Patents
notes.explanation: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) grant creators exclusive legal rights over innovations, technical designs, and corporate identity.
definitions: An exclusive legal right granted for an invention that is novel, non-obvious, and useful, typically valid for 20 years.
notes.example: A software algorithm combined with specialized hardware to improve energy efficiency can be patented if it passes novelty and utility requirements.
exam_points: Patents in India are governed by the Patents Act, 1970.
Term of patent protection is 20 years from the filing date.

notes.title: Copyrights & Trademarks
notes.explanation: Copyright protects literary, artistic, and computational works, while trademarks protect brand symbols, titles, and logos.
definitions: Exclusive economic and moral right given to authors over literary and artistic creations.
A distinctive sign, mark, or symbol identifying goods or services of a business entity.
notes.example: Source code of a modern software package is protected automatically under copyright upon creation.
exam_points: In India, general literary copyright duration is lifetime of author plus 60 years.
Trademarks can be renewed indefinitely every 10 years.

questions: Explain the jurisdictional challenges in Cyberspace with reference to the Sliding Scale Theory.
Discuss the extraterritorial provisions under the IT Act, 2000.
Define cyber stalking and identity theft. Discuss the relevant legal provisions under Indian IT Act.
What is data protection? Explain the self-regulation approach to privacy on the internet.
What are Intellectual Property Rights? Explain the macroeconomic impact of the patent system.
Outline the step-by-step process of filing and granting a patent in India.
Differentiate between Copyright and Trademarks with suitable examples.
Explain what constitutes trademark infringement and how trademarks are registered.

quiz.question: Which legal theory categorizes websites as passive, interactive, or commercial to determine jurisdiction?
quiz.explanation: The Sliding Scale Theory (Zippo test) categorizes web functionality to establish personal jurisdiction.

quiz.question: Under the Indian Patents Act, what is the standard validity period of a granted patent?
quiz.explanation: Patents are granted for a statutory term of 20 years from the date of filing.

subjects.name: Machine Learning
objectives: CO1: Define the concept of machine learning.
CO2: Outline the key characteristics of machine learning algorithms.
CO3: Compare the performance of different machine learning algorithms.
CO4: Design solution for basic problems using machine learning algorithms.
CO5: Explain the concept of reinforcement learning.

syllabus.topics: What is Machine Learning, Unsupervised Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Machine Learning Use-Cases, Machine Learning Process Flow, Machine Learning Categories, Linear regression and Gradient descent.

Classification and its use cases, Decision Tree, Algorithm for Decision Tree Induction, Creating a Perfect Decision Tree, Confusion Matrix, Random Forest. What is Naïve Bayes, How Naïve Bayes works, Implementing Naïve Bayes Classifier, Support Vector Machine, Illustration how Support Vector Machine works, Hyper parameter Optimization, Grid Search Vs Random Search, Implementation of Support Vector Machine for Classification.
What is Clustering & its Use Cases, K-means Clustering, How does K-means algorithm work, C-means Clustering, Hierarchical Clustering, How Hierarchical Clustering works.

Why Reinforcement Learning, Elements of Reinforcement Learning, Exploration vs Exploitation dilemma, Epsilon Greedy Algorithm, Markov Decision Process (MDP), Q values and V values, Q – Learning, α values.

notes.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals & Regression
notes.explanation: Machine Learning builds statistical models from input data to enable automated predictions without explicit rule programming. Linear regression models continuous values using Gradient Descent optimization.
definitions: An iterative optimization algorithm used to minimize the cost function by adjusting model parameters in the direction of steepest descent.
notes.example: House price prediction based on square footage using Linear Regression model y = wx + b.
exam_points: Supervised learning relies on labeled training data.
Learning rate (α) controls step size in gradient descent.

notes.title: Supervised Learning Classification
notes.explanation: Classification predicts discrete categorical labels. Algorithms include Decision Trees, Random Forests, Naïve Bayes, and Support Vector Machines (SVM).
definitions: A performance measurement table containing True Positives, True Negatives, False Positives, and False Negatives.
A supervised model finding an optimal decision hyperplane maximizing the margin between classes.
notes.example: Email spam classification using Naïve Bayes based on conditional probability calculations.
exam_points: Grid Search evaluates all parameter combinations; Random Search samples them randomly.
Naïve Bayes assumes independence between features given the class.

notes.title: Unsupervised Learning & Clustering
notes.explanation: Clustering partitions unlabelled data points into cohesive groups based on geometric distance metrics.
definitions: An iterative partitioning algorithm that minimizes the sum of squared distances between data points and cluster centroids.
notes.example: Customer segmentation in retail stores based on purchasing habits using Hierarchical Clustering.
exam_points: K-Means requires pre-specifying the number of clusters K.
Dendrograms visualize hierarchical clustering steps.

notes.title: Reinforcement Learning & MDP
notes.explanation: Reinforcement learning optimizes decision-making by training agents through rewards and penalties within interactive environments.
definitions: A model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the quality of actions (Q-values) in given Markov states.
notes.example: Training an autonomous game bot using Epsilon-Greedy policies to balance exploration and exploitation.
exam_points: Epsilon-greedy trades off exploring new actions vs exploiting best-known actions.
MDP framework consists of States, Actions, Transitions, and Rewards.

questions: Explain Linear Regression with mathematical formulation of Gradient Descent.
Differentiate between Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning with examples.
Construct a Confusion Matrix and derive Precision, Recall, and F1-Score formulas.
Compare Support Vector Machines and Decision Trees. Explain Hyperparameter tuning using Grid Search.
State the step-by-step algorithm for K-Means clustering. How are initial centroids selected?
Differentiate between Agglomerative and Divisive Hierarchical Clustering.
Explain the Exploration vs Exploitation dilemma in Reinforcement Learning.
Formulate Markov Decision Process (MDP) and derive the Q-Learning update rule.

quiz.question: Which evaluation metric matrix summarizes TP, TN, FP, and FN in classification tasks?
quiz.explanation: A Confusion Matrix visually details classification accuracy across True/False Positives and Negatives.

quiz.question: Which reinforcement learning parameter balances exploration versus exploitation in Epsilon-Greedy selection?
quiz.explanation: Epsilon (ε) dictates the probability of choosing a random action for exploration versus selecting the greedy choice.

subjects.name: Major Project
objectives: CO1: Integrate theoretical software engineering concepts into practical, working software systems.
CO2: Perform requirements gathering, system design, architectural modeling, and automated data store integration.
CO3: Deploy, test, and present capstone software solutions using modern frameworks and tools.

syllabus.topics: Project Selection, Requirements Analysis, System Architecture Specification, UI/UX Wireframing, Database Design & API Routing.
Core Implementation, Frontend-Backend Integration, Data Validation, Security Standards, Testing & Deployment.

notes.title: Capstone Software Lifecycle
notes.explanation: Major projects follow structured Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) models using modern tech stacks (e.g., Python/FastAPI/React).
definitions: Software Requirements Specification defining full functional and technical parameters of the application.
notes.example: Building an AI-assisted RAG Knowledge Base using web APIs and vector storage engines.
exam_points: Modular architecture ensures maintainability.
Version control (Git/GitHub) tracks code modifications.

questions: Draft an architectural design document and ER diagram for a scalable web application.
Detail unit testing, integration testing, and deployment workflows for project delivery.

quiz.question: Which document formally outlines functional requirements, non-functional constraints, and system design for software projects?
quiz.explanation: Software Requirements Specification (SRS) establishes formal requirements prior to implementation.

subjects.name: Mentorship and Professional Development (MPD)
objectives: CO1: Enhance professional communication, resume design, and interview readiness.
CO2: Build ethics, corporate etiquette, teamwork dynamics, and career planning strategies.

syllabus.topics: Resume Building, Technical Cover Letters, Mock Technical Interviews, Public Speaking & Group Discussions.
Workplace Etiquette, Professional Ethics, Time Management, Leadership & Team Collaboration.

notes.title: Career Readiness & Soft Skills
notes.explanation: Focuses on developing career portfolios, professional profiles, ATS-friendly resumes, and effective interpersonal skills.
definitions: Formatting a resume to ensure applicant tracking systems accurately parse technical skills and work experience.
notes.example: Structuring technical resume highlights using quantifiable achievements (e.g., optimized API latency by 30%).
exam_points: Tailor skill keywords to specific technical job postings.
Maintain clear structure and formatting.

questions: Describe key structural components of a professional ATS-optimized resume.
Explain essential strategies for participating effectively in Group Discussions.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) in modern recruitment processes?
options: Automated resume parsing, keyword matching, and screening
quiz.explanation: ATS platforms automatically parse and score incoming resumes against specified job descriptions.

subjects.name: Discrete Structures & Optimization
objectives: CO1: Apply mathematical logic, set theory, and discrete structures to model computer science problems.
CO2: Analyze algebraic structures, graph theory concepts, and optimization techniques for software solutions.

syllabus.topics: Mathematical Logic, Propositional and Predicate Logic, Sets, Relations, Functions, Equivalence Relations, Partial Orders, Lattice Theory.
Algebraic Structures, Groups, Subgroups, Rings, Fields, Combinatorics, Recurrence Relations, Generating Functions.
Graph Theory, Eulerian and Hamiltonian Graphs, Planar Graphs, Graph Coloring, Trees, Minimal Spanning Trees, Shortest Path Algorithms.
Optimization Techniques, Linear Programming Problem (LPP), Simplex Method, Transportation and Assignment Problems.

notes.title: Mathematical Logic & Posets
notes.explanation: Mathematical logic forms the core of program verification and automated reasoning, evaluating truth values via logical connectives and quantifiers.
definitions: A partially ordered set (poset) in which every pair of elements has a unique least upper bound (join) and greatest lower bound (meet).
A binary relation that is simultaneously reflexive, symmetric, and transitive on a set.
notes.example: Determining logical validity of compound propositions using truth tables and inference rules.
exam_points: Hasse diagrams visually represent finite partially ordered sets.
Equivalence relations partition a set into disjoint equivalence classes.

notes.title: Algebraic Structures & Combinatorics
notes.explanation: Algebraic structures define set system properties under binary operations, while generating functions solve linear recurrence relations.
definitions: An algebraic structure (G, *) satisfying closure, associativity, identity element presence, and inverse element presence.
notes.example: Solving the homogeneous recurrence relation a_n = 5a_{n-1} - 6a_{n-2} using characteristic equations.
exam_points: A Group becomes an Abelian Group if it additionally satisfies the commutative property.

notes.title: Graph Theory & Spanning Trees
notes.explanation: Graphs model networks, relationships, and state spaces. Spanning trees connect all vertices using a minimal subset of edges.
definitions: A closed graph trail containing every edge of a graph exactly once.
A graph that can be drawn in a single plane such that no two edges intersect each other.
notes.example: Applying Dijkstra's Algorithm to determine short-path routing trees across weighted networks.
exam_points: Euler's formula for connected planar graphs states V - E + R = 2.
Kruskal's algorithm selects minimum weight edges globally using disjoint sets.

notes.title: Optimization & Linear Programming
notes.explanation: Linear programming maximizes or minimizes objective functions under defined linear inequality constraints.
definitions: An iterative algebraic procedure for solving linear programming problems by testing vertex solutions on a convex polytope.
notes.example: Formulating resource allocation problems into standard canonical LPP matrices for Simplex execution.
exam_points: Transportation problems require balanced supply and demand conditions for initial feasible solutions.

questions: State and prove whether a given poset is a Lattice using Hasse diagram representation.
Construct a truth table to verify the logical equivalence of (p → q) and (¬p ∨ q).
Define Subgroup and state Lagrange's Theorem for finite groups.
Solve the recurrence relation a_n - 7a_{n-1} + 10a_{n-2} = 0 with initial conditions a_0 = 1, a_1 = 2.
Differentiate between Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs with suitable examples.
Explain Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms for finding Minimum Spanning Trees with complexity comparisons.
Solve the given Linear Programming Problem using the Simplex Method to maximize Z = 3x_1 + 5x_2.
Describe the Hungarian Method for solving optimal Assignment Problems.

quiz.question: Which property must a set relation satisfy to qualify as a Partial Order?
quiz.explanation: A Partial Order relation must be reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive.

quiz.question: What is the relation between Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Regions (R) in connected Planar Graphs according to Euler's formula?
quiz.explanation: Euler's planar formula dictates V - E + R = 2.

quiz.question: An algebraic group (G, *) that satisfies the commutative property is called a(n):
quiz.explanation: Abelian groups satisfy commutativity where a * b = b * a for all elements.

quiz.question: Which optimization technique relies on slack and surplus variables to find optimal vertex solutions?
quiz.explanation: The Simplex Method uses slack and surplus variables to turn inequalities into canonical matrix equations.

quiz.question: A connected graph without any cycles is formally classified as a:
quiz.explanation: A tree is defined as an acyclic, connected undirected graph.

subjects.name: Programming in Python
objectives: CO1: Understand core Python control flows, data structures, and object-oriented programming.
CO2: Utilize module libraries and file management techniques for software implementation.

syllabus.topics: Python Basics, Syntax, Data Types, Variables, Operators, Control Flow (If-Else, Loops), Functions, Scope, Lambda Expressions.
Built-in Data Structures: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, Sets, String Manipulation, Pattern Matching, List Comprehensions.
Object-Oriented Programming in Python: Classes, Objects, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation, Exception Handling.
File I/O Handling, Working with CSV and JSON data, Overview of Standard Libraries (NumPy, Pandas, OS, Sys modules).

notes.title: Python Control Flow & Functions
notes.explanation: Python features readable indentation syntax, dynamic typing, first-class functions, and anonymous lambda expressions.
definitions: An inline, anonymous function expressed as lambda arguments: expression.
notes.example: square = lambda x: x ** 2
exam_points: Python uses whitespace indentation rather than braces to define code blocks.

notes.title: Built-in Data Structures
notes.explanation: Python provides optimized sequence and mapping structures including mutable lists and dictionaries alongside immutable tuples.
definitions: A compact expression syntax used to create new lists from existing iterables.
notes.example: evens = [x for x in range(20) if x % 2 == 0]
exam_points: Dictionary keys must be of an immutable data type (e.g., strings, numbers, or tuples).

notes.title: Object-Oriented Programming & Exceptions
notes.explanation: OOP structures code into reusable class definitions featuring method overriding, encapsulation, and robust exception handlers.
definitions: Restricting direct access to an object's internal state using private attributes prefixed with underscores.
notes.example: Handling runtime file errors using try, except, else, and finally blocks.
exam_points: All instance methods in Python classes require 'self' as their first explicit parameter.

notes.title: File I/O & Scientific Libraries
notes.explanation: File handlers process persistent disk files, CSV structures, and JSON strings alongside numerical processing libraries.
definitions: A 2D tabular, column-oriented data structure with labeled axes for analytical processing.
notes.example: import pandas as pd; df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
exam_points: Use the 'with open()' context manager to ensure safe closing of file handles.

questions: Explain conditional logic and loop control statements (break, continue, pass) in Python with examples.
What are Lambda functions? Compare anonymous functions with standard def function definitions.
Compare Python Lists, Tuples, Sets, and Dictionaries based on mutability, indexing, and performance.
Demonstrate List Comprehensions and Dictionary Comprehensions with practical code examples.
Explain the concepts of Single, Multiple, and Multilevel Inheritance in Python.
Describe Python's Exception Handling architecture using try, except, raise, and custom exceptions.
Explain how to read, write, and manipulate JSON and CSV files in Python.
Discuss core capabilities of NumPy arrays and Pandas DataFrames in analytical applications.

quiz.question: Which of the following data structures in Python is immutable?
quiz.explanation: Tuples are immutable sequences whose elements cannot be changed post-creation.

quiz.question: What is the output of the Python expression: [x * 2 for x in range(3)]?
quiz.explanation: range(3) produces 0, 1, 2. Multiplying each element by 2 yields [0, 2, 4].

quiz.question: Which block in Python exception handling is guaranteed to execute regardless of whether an exception occurred?
quiz.explanation: The finally block always runs after try/except processing finishes.

quiz.question: Which keyword is mandatory as the first explicit parameter for instance methods inside a Python class definition?
quiz.explanation: Instance methods in Python implicitly bind the active object to the first parameter named self.

quiz.question: Which Python context manager ensures that persistent disk file handles automatically close upon code exit?
quiz.explanation: The 'with open()' statement opens a context manager that closes the file stream reliably.

subjects.name: Advanced Data Structures
objectives: CO1: Design advanced data structures including balanced search trees, heaps, and hash structures.
CO2: Evaluate asymptotic complexity of complex algorithmic procedures.

syllabus.topics: Asymptotic Analysis, Recurrence Relations, Stacks, Queues, Linked Lists, Circular & Doubly Linked Lists.
Tree Structures: Binary Search Trees (BST), AVL Trees, Red-Black Trees, B-Trees, B+ Trees, Segment Trees.
Heap Structures: Binary Heaps, Fibonacci Heaps, Priority Queues, Hashing Techniques, Hash Functions, Collision Resolution Methods.
Graph Algorithms: Topological Sorting, Strongly Connected Components, Disjoint Set Union (DSU), Dynamic Programming Data Structures.

notes.title: Linear Structures & Complexity
notes.explanation: Asymptotic analysis evaluates algorithmic time and space upper bounds. Linear structures manage dynamic sequential memory access.
