Industrial policy, Fiscal and Monetary policy, Public sector, Privatization, Globalization.
Consumer Protection Act, Competition Act, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Business Ethics.
Balance of Payments, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), World Trade Organization (WTO), Multinational Corporations.

notes.title: Macro-Environmental Forces
notes.explanation: Businesses operate within dynamic political, economic, socio-cultural, technological, environmental, and legal (PESTEL) macro frameworks.
definitions: The monitoring and evaluation of sweeping external trends and forces influencing organizational strategy.
notes.example: Assessing how central bank monetary rate hikes impact corporate borrowing costs.
exam_points: Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG reforms of 1991) transformed the Indian business landscape.

questions: Discuss the impact of LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) reforms on Indian business.
Explain the role of Fiscal and Monetary policies in controlling economic inflation and business cycles.

quiz.question: Which reform paradigm was formally introduced in India in July 1991?
quiz.explanation: India introduced sweeping structural economic reforms (LPG) in 1991 to open up markets.

subjects.name: Organizational Behaviour
objectives: CO1: Analyze human behavior in organizational settings across individual, group, and structural levels.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Organizational Behaviour, Nature, scope, foundations, perception, personality, values, attitudes.
Motivation concepts and theories (Maslow, Herzberg, Vroom), Job satisfaction, Leadership styles and theories.
Group dynamics, group development stages, team building, conflict management, negotiation strategies.
Organizational culture, organizational change, stress management, power and politics.

notes.title: Individual & Group Dynamics
notes.explanation: Organizational behaviour examines how human actions, perceptions, and attitudes affect enterprise productivity and team synergy.
definitions: The capacity to be aware of, control, and express one's emotions, and to handle interpersonal relationships judiciously.
notes.example: Applying Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory to improve employee retention and job satisfaction.
exam_points: Maslow's hierarchy of needs progresses from physiological safety needs up to self-actualization.

questions: Compare Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs with Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory of motivation.
Discuss leadership styles. Contrast transactional leadership with transformational leadership.

quiz.question: Which motivation theory categorizes workplace factors into 'Hygiene factors' and 'Motivators'?
quiz.explanation: Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory distinguishes hygiene maintenance factors from true motivational satisfiers.

subjects.name: Marketing Management
objectives: CO1: Formulate marketing strategies using the 4Ps and market segmentation analysis.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Marketing, Core concepts, Marketing management philosophies, Marketing Environment, Consumer Behavior.
Market Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP), Product Life Cycle (PLC), Branding, Packaging decisions.
Pricing strategies and methods, Distribution channels, Wholesaling, Retailing, Logistics management.
Promotional mix, Advertising, Sales promotion, Personal selling, Public relations, Digital marketing trends.

notes.title: Marketing Mix & Strategy
notes.explanation: Marketing management plans and executes conceptions, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services.
definitions: The foundational tactical toolset comprising Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.
notes.example: Developing STP (Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning) strategies for launching a new consumer electronic device.
exam_points: The Product Life Cycle (PLC) spans Introduction, Growth, Maturity, and Decline phases.

questions: Explain the Marketing Mix (4Ps). How is it expanded to 7Ps for services marketing?
Describe the stages of the Product Life Cycle (PLC) and formulate marketing strategies for each phase.

quiz.question: Which elements constitute the traditional Marketing Mix (4Ps)?
quiz.explanation: The traditional marketing mix formulated by E. Jerome McCarthy consists of Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.

subjects.name: Business Organization and Management
objectives: CO1: Describe fundamental concepts, nature and principles of Management.
CO2: Comprehend the role and responsibilities of managers and adapt to various styles of management.
CO3: Develop abilities to plan various business functions.
CO4: Apply various tools that would facilitate the decision making process in the business.
CO5: Determine different types of organizational structures and factors influencing organizational design.

syllabus.topics: Management: Meaning, definitions, nature, scope, functions, managerial roles and skills, basic forms of organizations (Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Joint stock company, HUF, Cooperative societies, trust). Evolution of management thoughts: scientific management, general administrative, quantitative, behavioral, systems, contingency approaches.

Planning: nature, scope, objectives, types of plans, planning process. Business forecasting, MBO. Decision Making: process, types, techniques. Social responsibility of business (CSR), Business ethics and ethical dilemmas.
Organizing: concept, nature, types, principles, process, formal/informal organizations, structures, departmentalization, authority, delegation, decentralization vs centralization, coordination.
Staffing: recruitment and selection process. Motivation: theories (Maslow, Herzberg, Theory X and Y, Vroom). Control: process, types, significance, span of control.

notes.title: Management Foundations & Forms of Business
notes.explanation: Management coordinates organizational resources through planning, organizing, leading, and controlling while operating within diverse legal business structures.
definitions: An approach pioneered by F.W. Taylor focusing on improving economic efficiency and labor productivity through standardized work methods.
notes.example: Comparing liability structures between Sole Proprietorships and Joint Stock Companies.
exam_points: Management is universal, dynamic, and combines both art and science principles.

notes.title: Planning, MBO & CSR
notes.explanation: Planning establishes future corporate direction, while CSR and ethics govern corporate accountability toward society.
definitions: A self-regulating business model enabling companies to be socially accountable to stakeholders and the public.
notes.example: Formulating MBO (Management by Objectives) targets for corporate sales divisions.
exam_points: Planning is a continuous, forward-looking intellectual process bridging current states to desired futures.

notes.title: Organizing, Authority & Decentralization
notes.explanation: Organizing frameworks establish clear reporting lines, delegation of authority, and departmental coordination.
definitions: The number of direct reports supervised efficiently by a single manager.
notes.example: Decentralizing operational decision-making authority from corporate headquarters to regional retail units.
exam_points: Delegation transfers authority and responsibility, but accountability remains ultimately with the manager.

notes.title: Staffing, Motivation & Control
notes.explanation: Staffing and motivation drive human capital productivity, while control mechanisms ensure adherence to performance standards.
definitions: A motivation model proposing that employee effort depends on expectancy, instrumentality, and valence.
notes.example: Applying Herzberg's hygiene factors to reduce employee turnover in manufacturing plants.
exam_points: Control systems act as feedback loops ensuring corrective action when actual performance deviates from plans.

questions: Discuss the evolution of management thought from classical scientific management to contingency theory.
Compare Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, and Joint Stock Company business entities.
Explain the planning process and discuss the significance of Management by Objectives (MBO).
What is Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)? Discuss arguments for and against corporate social obligations.
Distinguish between centralization and decentralization of authority. What factors influence the span of control?
Explain the principles of organizing and differentiate between line and staff authority.
Compare Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs and Herzberg's Two-Factor theory of motivation.
Explain the control process and discuss effective techniques of managerial control.

quiz.question: Who is known as the father of Scientific Management?
quiz.explanation: F.W. Taylor pioneered scientific management principles focusing on task efficiency and time-motion studies.

quiz.question: What does MBO stand for in management terminology?
quiz.explanation: MBO stands for Management by Objectives, a collaborative goal-setting framework.

quiz.question: What management term describes the number of subordinates directly reporting to a single superior?
quiz.explanation: Span of control defines the optimal number of direct reports per manager.

quiz.question: Which motivation theory incorporates Expectancy, Instrumentality, and Valence?
quiz.explanation: Vroom's Expectancy Model links effort, performance outcomes, and reward attractiveness.

quiz.question: Which business form features members with limited liability and separate legal entity status?
quiz.explanation: Joint Stock Companies possess separate legal entity status and limited shareholder liability.

subjects.name: Financial Accounting
objectives: CO1: Understand basic underlying concepts, principles and conventions of accounting.
CO2: Get an overview of the regulatory framework of accounting in India.
CO3: Understand the accounting framework of sole proprietorship and partnership firms.
CO4: Get acquainted with accounting frameworks of Royalty, Joint Venture, Consignment, Departments and Branches.

syllabus.topics: Basics of Accounting: Book-Keeping, accounting equation, accounting cycle (Journal, Ledger, Trial Balance), subsidiary books. GAAP, Capital vs Revenue expenditures. Financial statements of Sole Proprietor and Partnership.
Joint Venture accounts, Royalty accounts, Consignment accounts (consignee commission, account sales, accounting treatment).
Voyage accounts (complete/incomplete voyages), Departmental accounts (apportionment of expenses, interdepartmental transfers, unrealized profit).
Branch accounts (Dependent and Independent branches, Stock and Debtors system, consolidated P&L and Balance Sheet).

notes.title: Accounting Principles & Financial Statements
notes.explanation: Financial accounting records monetary business transactions systematically to prepare financial statements adhering to GAAP.
definitions: An accounting convention where every transaction impacts at least two accounts with equal debit and credit entries.
notes.example: Preparing income statements and balance sheets for sole proprietorship businesses with year-end adjustments.
exam_points: Capital expenditures yield long-term benefits, whereas revenue expenditures maintain daily operations.

notes.title: Joint Ventures, Consignments & Royalties
notes.explanation: Specialized accounts manage temporary joint ventures, goods consigned for sale, and periodic royalty payments.
definitions: An arrangement where goods are shipped by a consignor to a consignee who sells them on commission.
notes.example: Calculating minimum rent and shortworking recoupment in coal mine royalty accounts.
exam_points: Consignment goods remain the property of the consignor until sold by the consignee.

notes.title: Voyage & Departmental Accounts
notes.explanation: Voyage and departmental accounts evaluate profitability across distinct shipping voyages or internal business units.
definitions: Profit included in unsold stock transferred between departments or branches that must be eliminated.
notes.example: Apportioning shared electricity and rent expenses across manufacturing and sales departments.
exam_points: Interdepartmental stock transfers require creating provisions for unrealized departmental profits.

notes.title: Branch Accounting Systems
notes.explanation: Branch accounting tracks decentralized operating units using dependent branch stock and debtor ledger systems.
definitions: A branch operating entirely under head office control receiving goods at invoice or cost price.
notes.example: Preparing branch stock accounts under the stock and debtors branch accounting system.
exam_points: Independent branches maintain independent double-entry books requiring trial balance consolidation.

questions: Explain Accounting Concepts and Conventions (GAAP). Distinguish between Capital and Revenue expenditures.
Describe the accounting cycle from Journal entry recording to Trial Balance preparation.
Distinguish between Consignment and Joint Venture. Explain accounting entries in the books of the consignor.
Explain royalty accounts, minimum rent, shortworkings, and the right of recoupment.
Explain the objectives and accounting procedure of Departmental Accounts with expense apportionment.
How are voyage accounts treated for complete versus incomplete voyages at financial year-end?
Differentiate between Dependent and Independent branches. Explain the Stock and Debtors system.
How are consolidated Profit & Loss accounts prepared for head offices and branches?

quiz.question: What type of account is a Consignment Account in the books of the consignor?
quiz.explanation: Consignment account acts as a nominal trading account determining profit or loss on consigned goods.

quiz.question: What is unrecouped shortworking in royalty accounts referred to as?
options: Written off as a loss to Profit and Loss account
quiz.explanation: Unrecouped shortworking past expiry limits is written off as an expense in the P&L account.

quiz.question: How are unrealized profits on stock transfers between departments treated?
options: Eliminated by creating a stock reserve provision
quiz.explanation: Stock reserves eliminate unrealized internal profits remaining in closing inventory.

quiz.question: Under the Stock and Debtors system for dependent branches, what account is opened to record branch expenses?
quiz.explanation: Branch Expenses account records cash remittances and expenses incurred by dependent branches.

quiz.question: Which accounting convention dictates anticipating no profits and providing for all possible losses?
quiz.explanation: Conservatism convention requires accounting caution by recording prospective losses immediately.

subjects.name: Managerial Economics
objectives: CO1: Explain fundamental concepts of managerial economics and apply them to decision-making.
CO2: Analyze consumer behavior using demand theory and indifference curve analysis.
CO3: Examine production and cost functions in short and long runs.
CO4: Interpret revenue concepts and demand elasticity.
CO5: Assess pricing strategies and market structures.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Managerial Economics: nature, scope, opportunity cost, incremental concept, scarcity. Demand analysis: demand function, determinants, elasticities (price, income, cross), demand forecasting techniques.
Indifference Curve Analysis: consumer equilibrium, properties. Production function: productivity, technology, short/long run, isoquants, producer equilibrium, returns to scale.
Theory of Cost: short and long run cost theory, modern theory of cost. Revenue curves: total, average, marginal revenue, relationship with demand elasticity.
Market Structure: Perfect competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic competition, Oligopoly (collusive and non-collusive pricing models).

notes.title: Demand Theory & Elasticity
notes.explanation: Managerial economics applies microeconomic principles to optimize business pricing, demand estimation, and resource allocation.
definitions: The economic value of the best alternative foregone when executing a decision.
notes.example: Using price elasticity of demand coefficients to forecast revenue impacts following price hikes.
exam_points: Demand elasticity measures consumer responsiveness to price, income, or substitute price fluctuations.

notes.title: Consumer Behaviour & Production Functions
notes.explanation: Indifference curves analyze consumer utility maximization, while production functions evaluate input-output factor combinations.
definitions: A curve showing all combinatorial input factor quantities yielding a constant level of output.
notes.example: Determining least-cost factor combinations at the point of tangency between isoquants and isocost lines.
exam_points: Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution (MRTS) diminishes as capital substitutes labor along an isoquant.

notes.title: Cost Theory & Revenue Curves
notes.explanation: Cost curves outline short- and long-run expenses, while revenue curves link total, average, and marginal receipts.
definitions: Cost theory emphasizing saucer-shaped short-run average variable costs and U-shaped long-run average cost curves.
notes.example: Plotting Marginal Revenue alongside Price Elasticity: $MR = P(1 - 1/e)$.
exam_points: Long-run average cost curves (LAC) envelop short-run average cost curves (SAC).

notes.title: Market Structures & Oligopoly Pricing
notes.explanation: Market structures dictate competitive dynamics, pricing power, and output determination across industries.
definitions: An oligopoly pricing model explaining price rigidity where competitors match price cuts but ignore price hikes.
notes.example: Analyzing price and output equilibrium under perfectly competitive versus monopolistic markets.
exam_points: A firm maximizes profit where Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost ($MR = MC$).

questions: Explain the nature and scope of Managerial Economics. Discuss the Opportunity Cost and Incremental principles.
What is demand elasticity? Explain price, income, and cross-price elasticities with business applications.
Explain consumer equilibrium using Indifference Curve Analysis and budget lines.
Discuss the Law of Returns to Scale using Isoquants and producer equilibrium conditions.
Compare traditional and modern theories of cost. Explain the shape of Long Run Average Cost (LAC) curves.
Derive the relationship between Total Revenue, Average Revenue, Marginal Revenue, and Price Elasticity of Demand.
Compare price and output determination under Perfect Competition and Monopoly.
Explain collusive and non-collusive oligopoly pricing models, highlighting Paul Sweezy's kinked demand curve.

quiz.question: What does a price elasticity of demand equal to zero signify?
quiz.explanation: Zero elasticity indicates quantity demanded remains completely unchanged regardless of price shifts.

quiz.question: At what point on an isoquant is the producer in equilibrium?
options: Where the isoquant is tangent to the isocost line
quiz.explanation: Producer equilibrium occurs at the tangency point between an isoquant and an isocost line.

quiz.question: What shape does the Long-Run Average Cost (LAC) curve typically exhibit?
quiz.explanation: LAC curves exhibit a characteristic U-shape due to economies and diseconomies of scale.

quiz.question: What profit-maximizing condition applies to firms across all market structures?
options: Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost (MR = MC)
quiz.explanation: Profit maximization occurs precisely where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.

quiz.question: Which oligopoly model accounts for sticky, rigid prices due to asymmetric competitor reactions?
quiz.explanation: Sweezy's kinked demand curve explains price rigidity under non-collusive oligopoly.

subjects.name: Cost Accounting
objectives: CO1: Understand cost accounting principles, cost classification, and preparation of cost sheets.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Cost Accounting: meaning, objectives, scope, advantages, cost concepts and classification. Material Control: purchasing procedures, inventory control levels (EOQ), pricing methods (FIFO, LIFO, Weighted Average).

Labour Cost Control: time keeping, time booking, wage payment systems (Halsey, Rowan, Piece rate), labor turnover. Overhead Accounting: classification, allocation, apportionment, absorption of overheads.
Methods of Costing: Unit/Output costing, Preparation of Cost Sheet. Job and Batch costing. Contract costing: accounting for uncompleted contracts, escalation clauses.
Process Costing: process losses, abnormal gains/losses, joint products and by-products. Operating costing (transport, hotel). Reconciliation of cost and financial accounts.

notes.title: Cost Concepts & Material Control
notes.explanation: Cost accounting classifies operational expenses and manages material inventories efficiently using Economic Order Quantity (EOQ).
definitions: The optimal order quantity minimizing total inventory holding and ordering costs: $EOQ = \sqrt{\frac{2DS}{H}}$.
notes.example: Calculating material issue pricing using FIFO versus Weighted Average inventory valuation methods.
exam_points: Fixed costs remain constant in total, whereas variable costs fluctuate directly with production output.

notes.title: Labour & Overhead Accounting
notes.explanation: Labor control systems track wage incentives, while overhead accounting apportions and absorbs indirect manufacturing costs.
definitions: A wage incentive scheme granting workers a bonus equal to 50% of time saved multiplied by hourly rates.
notes.example: Apportioning factory rent and maintenance overheads across production service departments.
exam_points: Overhead absorption rates apply indirect manufacturing expenses to production units.

notes.title: Cost Sheets, Job & Contract Costing
notes.explanation: Cost sheets summarize cumulative production costs, while contract costing tracks long-term construction projects.
definitions: A contract clause protecting contractors against material and labor price inflation hikes.
notes.example: Preparing multi-tier cost sheets detailing prime cost, factory cost, cost of production, and total cost.
exam_points: Notional profit on uncompleted contracts requires cautious recognition based on cash received percentages.

notes.title: Process Costing & Reconciliation
notes.explanation: Process costing manages continuous manufacturing flows, and account reconciliation bridges cost and financial profits.
definitions: Loss exceeding normal expected process wastage due to machine breakdowns or operational inefficiencies.
notes.example: Reconciling profit discrepancies caused by pure financial expenses in cost and financial ledgers.
exam_points: Normal process loss is absorbed by surviving good production units, whereas abnormal loss is debited to costing P&L.

questions: Distinguish between Financial Accounting and Cost Accounting. Explain classification of costs.
Derive the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) formula and calculate inventory reorder levels.
Compare Halsey and Rowan premium wage incentive plans with numerical examples.
Explain the primary steps in overhead apportionment and absorption.
Prepare a comprehensive Cost Sheet showing Prime Cost, Works Cost, Cost of Production, and Total Cost.
Explain contract costing principles. How is notional profit calculated on uncompleted contracts?
Explain treatment of normal loss, abnormal loss, and abnormal gain in Process Costing.
Why do cost and financial accounts show different profit figures? Prepare a reconciliation statement.

quiz.question: What formula calculates Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)?
quiz.explanation: EOQ is calculated as the square root of twice annual demand times ordering cost divided by holding cost.

quiz.question: Under the Halsey premium plan, what percentage of time saved is typically paid as a bonus to the worker?
quiz.explanation: The standard Halsey plan pays a bonus equal to 50% of the time saved.

quiz.question: How is normal process loss treated in process costing calculations?
options: Credited to costing P&L as abnormal gain
Absorbed by good units produced, with scrap value credited to the process account
Debited directly to finished goods inventory
quiz.explanation: Normal loss is absorbed by good output units, and any scrap value reduces process costs.

quiz.question: What component is added to Works Cost to calculate Cost of Production?
quiz.explanation: Office and administrative overheads added to works cost yield the cost of production.

quiz.question: Which item is recorded exclusively in financial accounts and excluded from cost accounts?
options: Loss on sale of fixed assets
quiz.explanation: Losses on asset sales and pure financial items are recorded exclusively in financial accounts.

subjects.name: Business Environment
objectives: CO1: Evaluate macro and micro environmental forces impacting business operations.

syllabus.topics: Concept, significance, nature of business environment, environmental scanning, economic systems (capitalist, socialist, mixed).
Industrial Policy, Fiscal and Monetary policy, Public sector, Privatization, Globalization (LPG reforms of 1991).
Consumer Protection Act, Competition Act, Corporate Social Responsibility, Business Ethics.
Balance of Payments, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), World Trade Organization (WTO), Multinational Corporations (MNCs).

notes.title: Macro-Environment & Economic Systems
notes.explanation: Businesses operate within dynamic political, economic, socio-cultural, and legal environments requiring rigorous environmental scanning.
definitions: The systematic monitoring and evaluation of external macroeconomic forces affecting corporate strategy.
notes.example: Analyzing mixed economic system policies governing public-private partnerships in India.
exam_points: Micro environment includes customers, suppliers, and competitors; macro environment includes PESTEL forces.

notes.explanation: Industrial and macroeconomic monetary policies shape domestic business expansion and global competitiveness.
definitions: The removal of government controls and licensing restrictions to encourage private enterprise participation.
notes.example: Assessing how central bank repo rate adjustments influence corporate borrowing costs.
exam_points: India's 1991 LPG reforms dismantled industrial licensing and opened markets to foreign trade.

notes.explanation: Regulatory frameworks like the Consumer Protection Act and Competition Act protect fair market practices and consumer rights.
definitions: Legislation establishing consumer rights to safety, information, choice, and redressal forums.
notes.example: Filing consumer grievance claims at district redresses forums for defective merchandise.
exam_points: The Competition Act prevents anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominant market positions.

notes.explanation: Global trade agreements, WTO regulations, and FDI flows integrate domestic economies into global marketplaces.
definitions: An investment made by a company or entity in one country into business interests located in another country.
notes.example: Evaluating WTO tariff reduction impacts on domestic export manufacturing industries.
exam_points: Balance of Payments (BOP) records all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

questions: Explain the significance of Environmental Scanning. Compare capitalist, socialist, and mixed economic systems.
Differentiate between micro and macro business environments with appropriate examples.
Discuss the impact of 1991 LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) reforms on Indian industry.
Explain the objectives and instruments of monetary and fiscal policies in controlling inflation.
Explain the salient features and consumer rights under the Consumer Protection Act.
How does the Competition Act prevent anti-competitive practices and monopolistic abuse?
Explain the role of the World Trade Organization (WTO) in regulating international trade.
Discuss the benefits and challenges of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) for developing economies.

quiz.question: Which economic system combines private enterprise with government planning and public sector participation?
quiz.explanation: A mixed economy integrates private market forces with state regulatory guidance.

quiz.question: In which year were the historic LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) economic reforms launched in India?
quiz.explanation: India introduced sweeping macroeconomic reforms in July 1991.

quiz.question: Which regulatory act replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act in India?
quiz.explanation: The Competition Act of 2002 replaced the older MRTP Act to foster competitive market practices.

quiz.question: What does Balance of Payments (BOP) record?
options: All economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world
Corporate tax payments made to governments
quiz.explanation: BOP summarizes international trade, capital flows, and financial transfers.

quiz.question: What organization acts as the global institutional arbiter of international trade disputes?
options: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
quiz.explanation: The WTO regulates international trade agreements and resolves trade disputes among member nations.

subjects.name: Management Accounting
objectives: CO1: Apply management accounting tools for financial analysis, budgeting, and decision-making.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Management Accounting: meaning, objectives, nature, scope, difference between financial and cost accounting. Financial Statement Analysis: comparative statements, common-size statements, trend analysis, Ratio Analysis (liquidity, solvency, profitability, turnover ratios).
Funds Flow Statement and Cash Flow Statement (as per AS-3). Marginal Costing: contribution, P/V ratio, break-even analysis, margin of safety, decision-making applications.
Budgetary Control: objectives, classification of budgets (flexible, cash, fixed budgets), Zero-Base Budgeting. Standard Costing: variance analysis (material and labor variances).
Responsibility Accounting. Divisional performance measurement (ROI, Residual Income). Management reporting principles and types of reports.

notes.title: Financial Statement & Ratio Analysis
notes.explanation: Management accounting provides financial data interpreted via ratio analysis to evaluate liquidity, solvency, and operational efficiency.
definitions: A liquidity ratio measuring a firm's ability to cover short-term obligations with short-term assets: $\frac{\text{Current Assets}}{\text{Current Liabilities}}$.
notes.example: Analyzing multi-year trend percentages and common-size balance sheets to evaluate capital structure stability.
exam_points: Liquidity ratios measure short-term debt-paying capacity, whereas solvency ratios evaluate long-term financial stability.

notes.title: Fund Flows, Cash Flows & Marginal Costing
notes.explanation: Cash flow statements track cash movements under AS-3, while marginal costing analyzes break-even points for tactical decisions.
definitions: The operational output level where total revenues exactly equal total costs, resulting in zero profit or loss.
notes.example: Calculating Margin of Safety to determine how much sales can drop before incurring operating losses.
exam_points: Cash flows are classified into operating, investing, and financing activities under AS-3.

notes.title: Budgetary Control & Standard Costing
notes.explanation: Budgets plan future financial operations, while standard costing variance analysis isolates material and labor cost deviations.
definitions: The monetary difference between standard cost specified for actual production and actual cost incurred.
notes.example: Preparing flexible manufacturing overhead budgets across 60%, 80%, and 100% capacity utilization tiers.
exam_points: Favorable variances occur when actual costs fall below standards or actual revenues exceed budgets.

notes.title: Responsibility Accounting & Performance Metrics
notes.explanation: Responsibility accounting delegates financial accountability to divisional managers evaluated using ROI and Residual Income.
definitions: Net operating income earned above a minimum required return on divisional operating assets.
notes.example: Evaluating divisional subunit performance using Return on Investment (ROI) and Economic Value Added (EVA).
exam_points: Responsibility centers are categorized into cost, revenue, profit, and investment centers.

questions: Distinguish between Financial Accounting, Cost Accounting, and Management Accounting.
Explain liquidity, solvency, and profitability ratios. Calculate Current Ratio, Quick Ratio, and Debt-Equity Ratio.
Explain the preparation of Cash Flow Statements in accordance with Accounting Standard 3 (AS-3).
Define Marginal Costing. Explain Contribution, P/V Ratio, Break-Even Point, and Margin of Safety.
Discuss Budgetary Control objectives. Prepare a flexible cash budget for varying production levels.
Explain Material Cost Variance (Usage and Price) and Labor Cost Variance with formulas.
Explain Responsibility Accounting. Compare Return on Investment (ROI) with Residual Income.
Discuss principles of effective management reporting and types of management reports.

quiz.question: What does a quick ratio (acid-test ratio) exclude from current assets?
quiz.explanation: Quick ratio excludes least liquid inventories and prepaid expenses from current assets.

quiz.question: Under AS-3, how are dividend payments classified in cash flow statements for a manufacturing company?
quiz.explanation: Dividend payments represent cash outflows from financing activities.

quiz.question: What formula calculates the Profit-Volume (P/V) ratio in marginal costing?
quiz.explanation: P/V ratio expresses contribution as a percentage of total sales revenue.

quiz.question: Which budget adjusts automatically for changes in actual activity or volume levels?
quiz.explanation: Flexible budgets adjust expense allowances dynamically across varying activity levels.

quiz.question: What performance metric measures net operating income earned above minimum required capital returns?
quiz.explanation: Residual income measures absolute dollar returns exceeding cost of capital hurdles.

subjects.name: Mercantile Law
objectives: CO1: Comprehend legal frameworks governing commercial business transactions, contracts, and partnerships in India.

syllabus.topics: Indian Contract Act, 1872: Nature of contract, offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity of parties, free consent, void agreements, performance of contracts, breach of contract and remedies, contingency and quasi-contracts.
Contract of Indemnity and Guarantee, Bailment and Pledge, Law of Agency: creation, duties, rights, termination of agency.
Sale of Goods Act, 1930: Formation of contract, conditions and warranties, transfer of ownership, performance of contract, unpaid seller rights.
Indian Partnership Act, 1932: Nature, formation, registration, rights and duties of partners, dissolution of firms. Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, 2008: salient features.

notes.title: Indian Contract Act, 1872
notes.explanation: The Indian Contract Act governs formation, validity, performance, and remedies for breach of commercial agreements.
definitions: An agreement enforceable by law created between competent parties with free consent and lawful consideration.
notes.example: Analyzing whether coercion, undue influence, fraud, or mistake vitiates free consent in contracts.
exam_points: All contracts are agreements, but all agreements (e.g., social agreements) are not enforceable contracts.

notes.title: Indemnity, Guarantee, Bailment & Agency
notes.explanation: Special contracts govern indemnifying losses, guaranteeing debts, bailing goods, and executing commercial agency duties.
definitions: A contract where one party promises to save the other from loss caused by the promisor or third party.
notes.example: Establishing surety obligations and co-surety contributions under contracts of guarantee.
exam_points: Bailment involves delivery of goods upon condition that they shall be returned when purpose is accomplished.

notes.title: Sale of Goods Act, 1930
notes.explanation: The Sale of Goods Act governs contracts where property in goods is transferred from sellers to buyers for a price.
definitions: The legal doctrine ('let the buyer beware') stating buyers must inspect goods before purchase.
notes.example: Evaluating implied conditions of merchantability and fitness in commercial sales.
exam_points: An unpaid seller possesses statutory rights over goods including lien, stoppage in transit, and resale.

notes.title: Indian Partnership Act & LLP Act
notes.explanation: Partnership laws regulate relations between co-owners carrying on business for profit, alongside modern LLP regulations.
definitions: A corporate business vehicle combining partnership flexibility with limited liability protection.
notes.example: Executing partner dissolution deeds and evaluating minor partner liability admissions.
exam_points: Non-registration of a partnership firm bars partners from filing suits against third parties or co-partners.

questions: Define Contract. What are the essential elements of a valid contract under the Indian Contract Act?
Explain the doctrine of Free Consent. Distinguish between Coercion, Undue Influence, Fraud, and Misrepresentation.
Distinguish between a Contract of Indemnity and a Contract of Guarantee.
Explain the rights and duties of a Bailor and Bailee. What are the modes of termination of agency?
Distinguish between Condition and Warranty. When does a breach of condition be treated as breach of warranty?
Who is an Unpaid Seller? Explain the rights of an unpaid seller against goods and the buyer personally.
Explain the essential elements of Partnership. What are the consequences of non-registration of a firm?
Discuss the salient features and incorporation framework of Limited Liability Partnerships (LLP) under the LLP Act, 2008.

quiz.question: According to Section 2(h) of the Indian Contract Act, what is a contract defined as?
options: A written promise supported by moral obligation
quiz.explanation: A contract is legally defined as an agreement enforceable by law.

quiz.question: What legal maxim means 'let the buyer beware' in the Sale of Goods Act?
quiz.explanation: Caveat emptor places the burden of inspecting goods upon the buyer.

quiz.question: In a contract of guarantee, what is the person to whom the guarantee is given called?
quiz.explanation: The creditor is the party to whom a guarantee is given for the debt of another.

quiz.question: What is the minimum number of partners required to form a partnership firm in India?
quiz.explanation: A partnership requires a minimum of 2 partners carrying on business for profit.

quiz.question: Under the LLP Act 2008, what is the minimum number of designated partners required to be individuals resident in India?
quiz.explanation: LLPs require at least two designated partners, of whom at least one must be resident in India.

subjects.name: Foundations of Management
objectives: CO1: Provide fundamental knowledge and exposure to concepts, theories, and practices in management.

syllabus.topics: Management: Meaning, definitions, nature, scope, functions, managerial roles and skills, evolution of management thought.
Planning: Nature, purpose, process, types of plans, Management by Objectives (MBO), Decision making techniques.
Organizing: Concepts, structures, span of control, authority, delegation, decentralization, staffing and motivation.
Controlling: Process, methods, TQM, emerging issues in management in a global scenario.

notes.title: Management Principles & Theories
notes.explanation: Management integrates organizational resources through systematic planning, organizing, leading, and controlling.
definitions: A collaborative goal-setting process between managers and staff to define targets and monitor performance.
notes.example: Applying Henry Fayol's administrative principles to restructure corporate communication channels.
exam_points: Mintzberg identified 10 managerial roles grouped into interpersonal, informational, and decisional categories.

notes.title: Planning & Decision Making
notes.explanation: Planning establishes the overarching goals and decision frameworks required to guide future organizational actions.
definitions: Long-term comprehensive planning defining organizational direction and resource allocation.
notes.example: Formulating 5-year corporate expansion plans using SWOT analysis matrices.
exam_points: Effective decision making follows rational steps: defining the problem, identifying criteria, weighing alternatives, and selecting solutions.

notes.title: Organizing & Staffing Structures
notes.explanation: Organizing establishes authority relationships, task specialization, and departmental reporting structures.
definitions: The number of direct subordinates reporting efficiently to a single manager.
notes.example: Transitioning from a tall hierarchical structure to a flat decentralized matrix organization.
exam_points: Decentralization distributes decision-making authority down lower organizational tiers.

notes.title: Controlling & Modern Trends
notes.explanation: Controlling monitors actual operational performance against standards and implements corrective adjustments.
definitions: An organization-wide effort instilling permanent awareness of continuous quality improvement.
notes.example: Implementing Six Sigma statistical quality control metrics across manufacturing lines.
exam_points: Feedback control measures outputs post-operation, whereas feedforward control anticipates deviations.

questions: Discuss the evolution of management thought from classical to modern contingency theories.
Explain Mintzberg's managerial roles with real-world corporate examples.
Define Planning and explain the steps involved in the planning process.
What is Management by Objectives (MBO)? Discuss its advantages and limitations in modern enterprises.
Distinguish between centralization and decentralization. What factors determine the span of control?
Compare functional, divisional, and matrix organizational structures.
Explain the control process and differentiate between feedback and feedforward controls.
Discuss the principles of Total Quality Management (TQM) and its relevance in global business.

quiz.question: Who introduced the 14 Principles of Administrative Management?
quiz.explanation: Henry Fayol established the classic 14 principles of administrative management.

quiz.question: What does MBO stand for in management theory?
quiz.explanation: MBO stands for Management by Objectives, a collaborative target-setting framework.

quiz.question: Which organizational structure groups employees based on specialized skills and functional areas like Finance, HR, and Marketing?
quiz.explanation: Functional structures group specialists by their specific professional areas.

quiz.question: What type of control measures output performance after the completion of an activity or process?
quiz.explanation: Feedback control evaluates historical performance post-execution to inform future adjustments.

quiz.question: Which management pioneer is famously associated with Scientific Management and time-motion studies?
quiz.explanation: F.W. Taylor pioneered scientific management principles focusing on operational efficiency.

subjects.name: Managerial Economics
objectives: CO1: Apply microeconomic concepts, theories, and techniques to managerial decision-making.

syllabus.topics: Nature and scope of managerial economics, demand analysis, elasticity of demand, demand forecasting.
Production function, short run and long run costs, economies of scale, production optimization.
Market structures: Perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly pricing.
Pricing practices, profit management, business cycles, inflation.

notes.title: Demand & Microeconomic Analysis
notes.explanation: Managerial economics applies economic theory to optimize business decisions regarding resource allocation and pricing.
definitions: The value of the next best alternative foregone when making a decision.
notes.example: Analyzing cross-price elasticity to set competitive pricing strategies for substitute products.
exam_points: Demand elasticity dictates whether price increases will raise or lower total revenue.

notes.title: Production & Cost Dynamics
notes.explanation: Production functions analyze physical input-output relationships across short-run and long-run cost horizons.
definitions: Cost advantages experienced by enterprises as scale of operation increases with output expansion.
notes.example: Calculating marginal cost curves to determine optimal plant production output.
exam_points: The Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns states that adding successive variable inputs eventually yields smaller output increments.

notes.title: Market Structures & Pricing
notes.explanation: Market structures determine price-setting power and competitive behavior across industry sectors.
definitions: Selling identical goods or services at different prices to different consumer segments.
notes.example: Evaluating oligopolistic price rigidity and kinked demand curves in automobile industries.
exam_points: A firm under perfect competition is a price taker, whereas a monopolist is a price maker.

notes.title: Pricing Practices & Macro Environment
notes.explanation: Pricing strategies and macroeconomic conditions like inflation directly impact corporate profit margins and business cycles.
definitions: A pricing method setting prices by adding a standard markup percentage to total unit costs.
notes.example: Adjusting corporate markup margins in response to economy-wide inflation indexes.
exam_points: Business cycles encompass alternating phases of economic expansion, peak, contraction, and trough.

questions: Explain the Law of Demand and its exceptions. Discuss methods of demand forecasting.
How is price elasticity of demand measured? Explain its significance in managerial pricing decisions.
State and explain the Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns with a production schedule.
Distinguish between internal and external economies of scale.
Compare price and output determination under Perfect Competition and Monopoly.
Explain the kinked demand curve model under oligopolistic market conditions.
Discuss various managerial pricing practices including cost-plus and skimming pricing.
How do business cycles and inflation affect corporate investment and profit management?

quiz.question: What does an elasticity of demand value greater than 1 indicate?
quiz.explanation: Demand is elastic when percentage change in quantity demanded exceeds percentage change in price.

quiz.question: Which market structure features a single seller with high barriers to entry and no close substitutes?
quiz.explanation: Monopoly describes markets controlled by a single supplier dominating unique goods.

quiz.question: What economic concept measures the benefit lost from rejecting the next best alternative?
quiz.explanation: Opportunity cost represents foregone benefits of alternative choices.

quiz.question: What pricing strategy involves setting an initially high price for innovative products before lowering it over time?
quiz.explanation: Price skimming captures early high-willingness-to-pay segments before broader market rollout.

quiz.question: In the short run, what law explains why marginal product eventually decreases as variable inputs increase?
quiz.explanation: The Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns dictates declining incremental output past optimal factor ratios.

subjects.name: Business Analytics for Decision Making
objectives: CO1: Utilize data-driven analytical frameworks and quantitative techniques to guide business decisions.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Business Analytics, descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics frameworks.
Data exploration, probability distributions, hypothesis testing, ANOVA, regression analysis.
Forecasting models, time series analysis, optimization techniques, linear programming.
Data visualization, business intelligence dashboards, decision tree modeling.

notes.title: Analytics Frameworks & Modeling
notes.explanation: Business analytics transforms raw enterprise data into actionable insights using quantitative modeling and statistical tools.
definitions: Statistical and machine learning techniques used to predict future outcomes based on historical data.
notes.example: Applying multiple linear regression to forecast quarterly sales based on promotional spend.
exam_points: Descriptive analytics answers what happened, predictive tells what will happen, and prescriptive tells what action to take.

notes.title: Statistical Testing & Regression
notes.explanation: Statistical hypothesis testing and regression models validate business assumptions and evaluate variable relationships.
definitions: The probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as the observed results, assuming the null hypothesis is true.
notes.example: Performing ANOVA testing to compare customer satisfaction scores across four different store branches.
exam_points: Rejecting the null hypothesis occurs when the calculated p-value falls below the significance threshold (e.g., 0.05).

notes.title: Forecasting & Optimization
notes.explanation: Time-series forecasting and linear programming optimize operational resource scheduling and inventory management.
definitions: A mathematical technique maximizing or minimizing a linear objective function subject to linear constraints.
notes.example: Optimizing factory production allocation to maximize profit subject to machine hour limitations.
exam_points: Time series decomposition separates trend, seasonal, cyclical, and random irregular components.

notes.title: Data Visualization & BI Dashboards
notes.explanation: Business intelligence dashboards and decision tree models communicate analytical findings clearly to executive stakeholders.
definitions: A flowchart-like tree structure modeling decisions and their possible consequences using branching splits.
notes.example: Building interactive Tableau executive dashboards tracking daily revenue and regional KPIs.
exam_points: Decision trees calculate node splits using metrics such as Gini Impurity or Information Gain.

questions: Explain the three pillars of Business Analytics: Descriptive, Predictive, and Prescriptive analytics.
How does data-driven decision making transform modern enterprise competitiveness?
Explain the steps in Hypothesis Testing. Distinguish between Type I and Type II errors.
Describe how multiple linear regression models are evaluated using R-squared and coefficients.
Explain time-series decomposition in forecasting seasonal sales data.
Formulate and solve a basic linear programming maximization problem.
Discuss the role of Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards in executive decision making.
Explain how Decision Tree classification models split data nodes.

quiz.question: Which branch of analytics focuses on determining optimal courses of action?
quiz.explanation: Prescriptive analytics recommends optimization strategies and best actions to achieve business goals.

quiz.question: What type of error occurs when a researcher rejects a true null hypothesis?
quiz.explanation: Type I error (alpha) represents false positives where a true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected.

quiz.question: Which analytical technique is used to model the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables?
quiz.explanation: Regression analysis estimates mathematical relationships between dependent and independent variables.

quiz.question: What mathematical technique optimizes resource allocation subject to given constraints?
quiz.explanation: Linear programming optimizes objective functions under strict linear boundary constraints.

quiz.question: What metric measures the proportion of variance in a dependent variable explained by a regression model?
quiz.explanation: R-squared represents the coefficient of determination measuring regression model goodness of fit.

subjects.name: Marketing Management
objectives: CO1: Develop marketing strategies through STP analysis and the marketing mix.

syllabus.topics: Marketing concepts, philosophies, marketing environment, consumer behavior analysis.
Market Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP), Product Life Cycle (PLC), branding decisions.
Pricing strategies, distribution channels, supply chain logistics management.
Promotional mix, advertising, digital marketing trends, customer relationship management.

notes.title: Marketing Strategy & STP
notes.explanation: Marketing management plans and executes creation, pricing, promotion, and distribution of goods and services.
definitions: The tactical marketing toolset comprising Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.
notes.example: Formulating STP strategies for launching a new consumer tech product line.
exam_points: The Product Life Cycle (PLC) spans Introduction, Growth, Maturity, and Decline stages.

notes.title: Product & Brand Management
notes.explanation: Product lifecycles and brand equity strategies dictate long-term market positioning and profitability.
definitions: The commercial value derived from consumer perception and goodwill associated with a brand name.
notes.example: Managing brand extensions and packaging designs for consumer packaged goods.
exam_points: During the maturity stage of a PLC, marketing focus shifts toward customer retention and product differentiation.

notes.title: Pricing & Distribution Channels
notes.explanation: Distribution channels and physical logistics ensure seamless product delivery from manufacturers to end consumers.
definitions: Managing the end-to-end flow of goods, warehousing, and transportation from origin to consumption.
notes.example: Establishing multichannel distribution networks integrating online e-commerce and retail stockists.
exam_points: Channel intermediaries reduce transaction complexities between producers and fragmented buyers.

notes.title: Promotion & Digital Marketing
notes.explanation: Integrated marketing communications combine advertising, digital campaigns, and CRM to build customer loyalty.
definitions: Coordinating all promotional tools and channels to deliver a unified brand message.
notes.example: Running synchronized social media influencer campaigns alongside programmatic digital display ads.
exam_points: Digital marketing analytics measure conversion rates, cost-per-click (CPC), and customer lifetime value (CLV).

questions: Explain Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning (STP) with corporate examples.
How do micro and macro environmental factors influence modern marketing strategies?
Discuss the stages of the Product Life Cycle (PLC) and appropriate marketing strategies for each phase.
What is brand equity? Explain strategies for building strong brand portfolios.
Compare direct and indirect distribution channels. What factors influence channel selection?
Explain various pricing strategies including value-based and competitive pricing.
Explain the components of the Promotional Mix and Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC).
Discuss emerging digital marketing trends and their impact on Customer Relationship Management (CRM).

quiz.question: What does STP stand for in marketing strategy?
quiz.explanation: STP stands for Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning.

quiz.question: Which stage of the Product Life Cycle typically experiences peak sales and intense market competition?
quiz.explanation: Maturity is characterized by peak sales adoption and saturated competitive pressures.

quiz.question: What marketing term describes the commercial value and consumer goodwill attached to a brand name?
quiz.explanation: Brand equity measures consumer perception value and preference strength for a brand.

quiz.question: Which channel intermediary structure involves zero intermediaries between manufacturer and customer?
quiz.explanation: Direct channels sell manufacturer goods directly to end users without intermediaries.

quiz.question: What concept ensures consistency across all advertising, PR, and digital promotional touchpoints?
quiz.explanation: IMC synchronizes promotional messages across all communication channels.

subjects.name: Organizational Behaviour
objectives: CO1: Analyze individual, group, and organizational dynamics to improve workplace performance.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to OB, personality, perception, values, attitudes, emotional intelligence.
Motivation theories (Maslow, Herzberg, Vroom), leadership styles and effectiveness.
Group dynamics, team building, conflict management, negotiation strategies.
Organizational culture, change management, stress management, power and politics.

notes.title: Human Dynamics & Motivation
notes.explanation: Organizational behaviour studies human action and interaction to enhance corporate productivity and workplace culture.
definitions: The ability to monitor one's own and other people's emotions and use information to guide thinking and actions.
notes.example: Applying Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory to design employee engagement and retention programs.
exam_points: Maslow's hierarchy progresses from physiological needs up to self-actualization.

notes.title: Motivation & Leadership
notes.explanation: Workplace motivation models and leadership styles dictate employee morale and organizational effectiveness.
definitions: Leadership inspiring followers to transcend self-interest and achieve extraordinary organizational outcomes.
notes.example: Using Vroom's Expectancy Theory to align performance bonuses with employee motivation.
exam_points: Transformational leaders inspire vision, whereas transactional leaders manage routine task performance.

notes.title: Group Dynamics & Conflict
notes.explanation: Teams progress through distinct developmental stages, requiring active conflict resolution and negotiation skills.
definitions: The second stage of group development characterized by intra-group conflict and resistance to constraints.
notes.example: Resolving cross-departmental project resource conflicts using collaborative negotiation.
exam_points: Tuckman's stages of group development include Forming, Storming, Norming, Performing, and Adjourning.

notes.title: Culture, Change & Stress Management
notes.explanation: Managing organizational culture, planned change initiatives, and workplace stress ensures long-term corporate resilience.
definitions: The shared values, beliefs, and norms governing how people behave in organizations.
notes.example: Implementing Lewin's 3-step change model (Unfreeze, Change, Refreeze) for digital transformation.
exam_points: Role ambiguity and workload overload represent primary occupational stress drivers.

questions: Explain the significance of Emotional Intelligence (EI) in modern management and leadership.
How do perception and personality traits influence workplace behavior and job satisfaction?
Compare Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs with Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory.
Discuss contemporary leadership styles including transformational and transactional leadership.
Explain Tuckman's Stages of Group Development with practical team-building examples.
Discuss conflict management strategies and win-win negotiation techniques.
Explain Kurt Lewin's 3-Step Change Model for managing organizational change.
What are the causes and coping mechanisms for managing occupational workplace stress?

quiz.question: Which theory categorizes work environment factors into hygiene factors and motivators?
quiz.explanation: Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory separates hygiene maintenance factors from true motivators.

quiz.question: What is the second stage in Tuckman's stages of group development?
quiz.explanation: Storming is characterized by conflict over control and task direction.

quiz.question: Which leadership style inspires followers to transcend self-interest for a shared organizational vision?
quiz.explanation: Transformational leaders motivate teams through vision, charisma, and intellectual stimulation.

quiz.question: What are the three steps in Kurt Lewin's organizational change model?
quiz.explanation: Lewin's model outlines Unfreezing current state, Changing, and Refreezing new behaviors.

quiz.question: Which emotional construct measures self-awareness, empathy, and social skill in interpersonal relationships?
quiz.explanation: Emotional intelligence encompasses self-awareness, emotional regulation, and social aptitude.

subjects.name: Marketing Research
objectives: CO1: Design, execute, and analyze market research projects to support managerial decisions.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to marketing research, research design, secondary and primary data collection methods.
Measurement and scaling techniques, questionnaire design, sampling design and procedures.
Data collection field work, data processing, univariate and bivariate statistical testing.
Multivariate data analysis techniques, research report writing and presentation.

notes.title: Research Design & Methodology
notes.explanation: Marketing research systematically gathers, records, and analyzes data concerning marketing problems to assist decision-making.
definitions: A framework or blueprint for conducting marketing research projects specifying data collection and analysis methods.
notes.example: Designing a Likert-scale customer satisfaction survey for a retail banking service.
exam_points: Primary data is collected firsthand for a specific research problem, whereas secondary data already exists.

notes.explanation: Valid survey instruments use structured scaling techniques and precise sampling designs to ensure data reliability.
definitions: A psychometric scale requiring respondents to indicate levels of agreement or disagreement with statements.
notes.example: Designing stratified random sampling frames to survey consumer electronics buyers across regions.
exam_points: Reliability measures instrument consistency, while validity measures whether it measures what it intends to measure.

notes.explanation: Fieldwork data processing and univariate/bivariate hypothesis testing extract meaningful statistical inferences.
definitions: A statistical test evaluating whether categorical frequencies differ significantly from expected theoretical distributions.
notes.example: Running independent sample t-tests to evaluate differences in brand preference scores across genders.
exam_points: Bivariate testing examines relationships between two variables using correlation and chi-square statistics.

notes.explanation: Advanced multivariate techniques and formal report presentations communicate complex research findings to stakeholders.
definitions: A multivariate statistical technique reducing a large set of correlated variables into fewer underlying dimensions.
notes.example: Using factor analysis to identify core consumer lifestyle dimensions from survey data.
exam_points: A formal research report must articulate executive summaries, methodology, findings, and managerial recommendations.

questions: Explain the steps involved in the Marketing Research Process.
Compare exploratory, descriptive, and causal research designs with business examples.
Discuss comparative and non-comparative scaling techniques used in questionnaire design.
Compare probability and non-probability sampling methods with business applications.
Explain the data editing, coding, and tabulation processes in marketing research.
When should you apply Chi-Square tests versus ANOVA in bivariate marketing data analysis?
Explain the application of Factor Analysis and Cluster Analysis in market segmentation research.
What are the key structural components of a professional research report?

quiz.question: Which data collection method involves gathering data firsthand specifically for the current research problem?
quiz.explanation: Primary data is collected directly by researchers for the specific study at hand.

quiz.question: What psychometric scale asks respondents to indicate their level of agreement on a 5- or 7-point continuum?
quiz.explanation: Likert scales measure attitudes by evaluating agreement levels across statement items.

quiz.question: Which sampling technique gives every element in the population an equal and known chance of selection?
quiz.explanation: Simple random sampling ensures unbiased probability selection across population frames.

quiz.question: What multivariate technique reduces a large number of correlated variables into fundamental underlying dimensions?
quiz.explanation: Factor analysis uncovers latent unobserved constructs from correlated survey variables.

quiz.question: What statistical test evaluates whether two or more categorical proportions differ significantly?
quiz.explanation: Chi-Square tests evaluate associations and goodness-of-fit across categorical frequency data.

B.Sc. ATHM.full_name: Bachelor of Science in Airlines, Tourism and Hospitality Management (B.Sc. ATHM )

subjects.name: Basics of Tourism
objectives: CO1: Comprehend the general and specific dynamics of global tourism industry components and systems.
CO2: Identify tourist motivations (McIntosh, Grey's wanderlust/sunlust) and travel market segments.
CO3: Analyze positive and negative economic, socio-cultural, and environmental impacts of tourism alongside carrying capacity.

syllabus.topics: Introduction: Leisure, recreation, and tourism relationship, travel lingo, classification of tourism by destination (international, domestic), purpose (cultural, business, VFR, pilgrimage), and mode of travel arrangement (inclusive, independent).
Motivation of Travel: Physical, cultural, interpersonal, status, and prestige motivations (McIntosh model), alongside Grey's Wanderlust and Sunlust motivations.

Global Tourism: Historical development across ancient/imperial eras, Roman, Greek, and Indian travelers, Silk Route, Grand Tours, Thomas Cook development, present scenario, and growth factors (technology, social patterns, living standards).

Barriers to Tourism & Domestic Tourism: Destination barriers (terrorism, political environment), tourist barriers (time, cost, social). Definition and significance of domestic tourism, positive/negative economic, socio-cultural, and environmental impacts.

Carrying Capacity & Sustainable Tourism: Physical, biological, and social carrying capacities. Eco-tourism definition, benefits, Agenda 21, promoting bodies, principles, and differences between mass and green tourism.

notes.title: Tourism Concepts & Classifications
notes.explanation: Tourism is an open economic system driven by temporary mobility and diverse travel motivations across domestic and international boundaries.
definitions: A primary tourism purpose category where travelers visit family or acquaintances.
notes.example: Differentiating an inclusive packaged holiday tour from an independently booked leisure trip.
exam_points: Excursionists are temporary visitors staying less than 24 hours without overnight accommodation.

notes.title: Travel Motivation Models
notes.explanation: Travel behavior is governed by psychological push factors categorized by McIntosh and Grey's wanderlust versus sunlust theories.
definitions: The basic human desire to leave the familiar environment and explore different cultures and destinations.
notes.example: Analyzing traveler motivations for undertaking pilgrimage tourism versus adventure sports holidays.
exam_points: Sunlust travel is motivated primarily by recreational relaxation in warmer sunny coastal climates.

notes.title: Evolution of Global Tourism
notes.explanation: Modern tourism expanded from early Silk Route exploration to Thomas Cook's pioneering 1841 railway excursions.
definitions: Historic educational travel undertaken by young European aristocrats across cultural capitals.
notes.example: Tracing the evolution of commercial travel from steamship networks to modern civil aviation.
exam_points: Rising disposable incomes and paid annual leave have catalyzed post-war global tourism growth.

notes.title: Impacts & Carrying Capacity
notes.explanation: Sustainable tourism planning balances economic foreign exchange gains against environmental degradation and socio-cultural carrying capacity limits.
definitions: The maximum threshold of visitor volume a destination can sustain without ecological or social damage.
notes.example: Enforcing daily tourist caps in fragile ecological sanctuaries to protect local wildlife habitats.
exam_points: Agenda 21 established global operational guidelines for sustainable ecotourism development.

questions: Classify tourism based on destination, purpose of visit, and mode of travel arrangements.
Discuss the relationship between leisure, recreation, and modern tourism.
Explain McIntosh's tourist motivation model and differentiate between Grey's wanderlust and sunlust.
Analyze the psychological push and pull factors influencing individual travel decisions.
Trace the historical development of global tourism from ancient explorers to Thomas Cook.
Discuss the technological and social factors driving contemporary global tourism growth.
Evaluate the positive and negative economic, socio-cultural, and environmental impacts of tourism.
Define carrying capacity and explain physical, biological, and social carrying capacities in sustainable destinations.

quiz.question: According to Stanley P. Grey, what type of travel motivation is driven by the desire for relaxation in sunny climates?
quiz.explanation: Sunlust refers to travel motivated by the search for recreational sunshine and relaxation away from home.

quiz.question: Who organized the first commercial railway excursion package in Britain in 1841?
quiz.explanation: Thomas Cook pioneered commercial packaged tourism by organizing a train excursion in Leicestershire.

quiz.question: What term refers to the maximum visitor threshold a destination can withstand without permanent environmental damage?
quiz.explanation: Carrying capacity defines ecological and social limits protecting destinations from over-tourism.

quiz.question: Which international action plan for sustainable development originated from the 1992 Rio Earth Summit?
quiz.explanation: Agenda 21 outlined comprehensive global strategies for achieving sustainable environmental development.

subjects.name: Tourism Product and Services - I
objectives: CO1: Understand the 5 A's of tourism products and differentiate between tangible products and intangible services.
CO2: Analyze the hotel accommodation sector and luxury tourist train networks across India.
CO3: Explore natural attractions, cultural heritage, and adventure sports activities in Indian tourism.

syllabus.topics: Introduction: Tangible and intangible products, product versus service differences, Tourism Product 5 A's (Accommodation, Accessibility, Attraction, Activities, Amenities).
Accommodation Sector: Hotel industry introduction in India, types of hotels, five-star hotels, leading hotel chains, budget hotels, and heritage hotels.

Transportation Sector: Indian transportation industry, roadways (national/state highways, expressways), railways, tourist trains (Palace on Wheels, Deccan Odyssey, Fairy Queen), domestic airlines, and national waterways.

Attractions: Natural attractions (mountains, beaches, forests, islands, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries), cultural attractions (fairs, festivals, paintings, museums, monuments, handicrafts, cuisines).

Activities: Winter and summer sports (mountaineering, trekking, skiing, skating), water-based sports (white water rafting, river crossing, angling, surfing, kayaking, boating, parasailing), aero sports (hang gliding, ballooning, bungee jumping).

notes.title: 5 A's of Tourism Products
notes.explanation: A complete tourism destination experience relies on the harmonious integration of the 5 A's: Attractions, Accessibility, Amenities, Accommodation, and Activities.
definitions: A complex composite of tangible components and intangible experiences centered on a destination.
notes.example: Combining hotel lodging, transport accessibility, and guided adventure activities into a unified tour package.
exam_points: Unlike manufactured goods, tourism products are perishable, intangible, and consumed where produced.

notes.title: Accommodation & Heritage Hotels
notes.explanation: The lodging sector ranges from luxury five-star business hotels to heritage palace properties preserving royal Indian history.
definitions: Historic palaces, castles, and forts converted into operating luxury hospitality accommodations.
notes.example: Operating heritage hotels in Rajasthan showcasing historic Rajput architecture and royal hospitality.
exam_points: Leading international and domestic hotel chains set standardized benchmarks for guest service quality.

notes.title: Transportation & Luxury Trains
notes.explanation: Seamless connectivity across India is supported by national highways, expressways, domestic aviation, and iconic luxury tourist trains.
definitions: A luxury tourist train operated by Indian Railways and RTDC showcasing royal heritage travel across Rajasthan.
notes.example: Booking luxury rail journeys like the Deccan Odyssey or Fairy Queen heritage steam locomotive.
exam_points: National highways and expressways connect major metropolitan tourism circuits across India.

notes.title: Attractions & Adventure Sports
notes.explanation: India offers diverse natural and cultural attractions alongside thrilling water, land, and aero adventure sports.
definitions: Outdoor leisure activities involving physical exploration and a calculated element of challenge and risk.
notes.example: Organizing white water rafting expeditions on the Ganges in Rishikesh or trekking in Himalayan passes.
exam_points: Wildlife sanctuaries and national parks protect endangered Indian fauna like the Bengal tiger and one-horned rhinoceros.

questions: Explain the 5 A's of tourism and distinguish between tangible products and intangible services.
Discuss how attractions and amenities collectively constitute a marketable tourism destination.
Trace the evolution of the hotel industry in India and classify luxury versus budget accommodation sectors.
Discuss the role and operational appeal of heritage hotels in Indian tourism.
Describe the role of Indian Railways and iconic luxury tourist trains in promoting cultural tourism.
Evaluate the contribution of roadways and domestic civil aviation to tourism accessibility in India.
Highlight major natural and cultural attractions that position India as a global tourism destination.
Discuss the scope and safety management of water-based and aero-adventure sports in India.

quiz.question: What luxury tourist train operates in collaboration with Indian Railways to showcase royal heritage across Rajasthan?
quiz.explanation: Palace on Wheels is the pioneer luxury tourist train launched to promote tourism across Rajasthan.

quiz.question: What do the 5 A's of tourism products include in destination planning?
quiz.explanation: The 5 A's represent Attractions, Accessibility, Amenities, Accommodation, and Activities.

quiz.question: Which adventure sport involves navigating fast-flowing river rapids using inflatable rafts?
quiz.explanation: White water rafting is a popular water-based adventure sport conducted on rapid river currents.

quiz.question: What accommodation category involves converting former royal palaces and stately homes into luxury hotels?
quiz.explanation: Heritage hotels are historic properties converted into hospitality venues preserving cultural architecture.

subjects.name: Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences
objectives: CO1: Apply foundational programming concepts in Python to solve pharmaceutical and biological data problems.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Python programming, data types, variables, operators, control structures, loops, functions.
Data structures in Python (Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, Sets), file handling, exception handling.
Introduction to scientific libraries: NumPy for numerical computing and Pandas for tabular pharmaceutical data manipulation.
Basic data visualization using Matplotlib and Seaborn for plotting experimental and clinical datasets.

notes.title: Python Syntax & Fundamentals
notes.explanation: Python provides a simple, readable syntax well-suited for automating calculations and processing laboratory datasets.
definitions: A reserved memory location storing numerical, string, or boolean data values.
notes.example: Writing a Python script to calculate molecular weight concentrations from input data strings.
exam_points: Python uses dynamic typing and indentation blocks instead of curly brackets.

questions: Explain the fundamental data types and control flow statements in Python.
Write a Python function to compute the mean and standard deviation of a list of absorbance readings.

quiz.question: Which Python library is primarily used for multidimensional array operations and numerical computing?
quiz.explanation: NumPy provides high-performance N-dimensional array objects and mathematical functions.

subjects.name: General Pharmacy
objectives: CO1: Understand the history, evolution, ethics, and professional scope of pharmacy practice.

syllabus.topics: History and evolution of pharmacy profession in India and globally, professional ethics and code of conduct.
Pharmacopoeias (IP, BP, USP, International Pharmacopoeia), sources of drug information, pharmaceutical calculations.
Introduction to dosage forms, prescription handling, Latin terms and abbreviations used in prescriptions.
Hospital and community pharmacy services, role of pharmacists in patient counseling and public health.

notes.title: History & Pharmacopoeias
notes.explanation: The pharmacy profession bridges chemical sciences and patient healthcare, regulated through international pharmacopoeial standards.
definitions: An official book containing directions for the identification of compound medicines published by statutory authority.
notes.example: Interpreting Latin prescription abbreviations such as 'bis in die' (twice a day).
exam_points: The Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP) sets official legal quality standards for drugs manufactured in India.

questions: Trace the history and evolution of the pharmacy profession in India.
Explain the significance of Pharmacopoeias in ensuring drug quality standards.

quiz.question: What does the Latin abbreviation 'bid' stand for in prescription reading?
quiz.explanation: 'bid' stands for bis in die, meaning twice a day.

subjects.name: Human Anatomy, Physiology and Pathophysiology I
objectives: CO1: Comprehend structural organization of the human body and physiological mechanisms of organ systems.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to human body, cellular level of organization, tissue level, integumentary system, skeletal system, joints.
Blood and lymphatic system: composition, blood groups, coagulation, immunity, pathophysiology of anemias.
Cardiovascular system: anatomy of heart, cardiac cycle, ECG, blood pressure, pathophysiology of hypertension and atherosclerosis.
Respiratory system: anatomy, mechanics of respiration, gas exchange, pathophysiology of asthma and COPD.

notes.title: Cellular Organization & Cardiovascular System
notes.explanation: Human physiology coordinates cellular homeostasis across cardiovascular, respiratory, and hematological organ systems.
definitions: The tendency toward a relatively stable equilibrium between interdependent physiological elements.
