subjects.name: Applied Thermodynamics
objectives: CO1: Analyze performance of vapor power cycles (Rankine cycle) and steam generators.
CO2: Evaluate reciprocating and rotary air compressors and gas turbine cycles.
CO3: Understand refrigeration cycles, psychrometric properties, and air conditioning processes.

syllabus.topics: Vapor Power Cycles: Carnot vapor cycle, Rankine cycle, effect of operating parameters (pressure and temperature) on Rankine cycle efficiency, reheat and regenerative Rankine cycles.

Steam Generators & Nozzles: Classification of boilers, boiler mountings and accessories, boiler efficiency. Steam nozzles: Isentropic flow through nozzles, critical pressure ratio, effect of friction.
Air Compressors: Reciprocating compressors, single and multistage compression, volumetric efficiency, intercooling. Rotary compressors: Centrifugal and axial flow compressors.
Gas Turbines & Refrigeration: Brayton cycle, regeneration, intercooling, reheat gas turbines. Vapor compression refrigeration cycle, refrigerants, psychrometry and psychrometric chart processes.

notes.title: Rankine Cycle & Vapor Power Systems
notes.explanation: The Rankine cycle is the thermodynamic backbone of thermal power plants generating electricity from steam.
definitions: The ratio of net work output to heat supplied in a vapor power cycle.
notes.example: Enhancing thermal power plant efficiency using regenerative feedwater heating and steam reheating.
exam_points: Increasing boiler pressure and superheating steam raise overall Rankine cycle thermal efficiency.

questions: Explain the Rankine vapor power cycle with P-v and T-s diagrams and derive its thermal efficiency.
Discuss methods to improve Rankine cycle efficiency (reheating and regeneration).

quiz.question: What ideal thermodynamic cycle serves as the standard benchmark for vapor power plants?
quiz.explanation: The Rankine cycle models vapor power generation processes involving phase change.

subjects.name: Fluid Machines
objectives: CO1: Understand principles of impulse and reaction hydraulic turbines.
CO2: Analyze performance characteristics and vector diagrams of centrifugal and reciprocating pumps.
CO3: Evaluate hydraulic machinery, draft tubes, and specific speed classifications.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Turbo-machinery: Impactor and reaction machines, impulse-momentum principle applied to blades, velocity triangles, work done and efficiency.
Hydraulic Turbines: Classification, Pelton turbine, Francis turbine, Kaplan turbine, velocity vector diagrams, work done, efficiencies, specific speed, draft tubes, governing of turbines.
Centrifugal Pumps: Working principle, classification, velocity triangles, manometric head, efficiencies, multistage pumps, specific speed, priming, pump characteristic curves, cavitation.
Reciprocating Pumps & Hydraulic Devices: Reciprocating pump mechanism, indicator diagrams, slip, effect of acceleration and friction, air vessels. Hydraulic accumulator, intensifier, hydraulic press.

notes.title: Pelton Turbine & Hydraulic Efficiency
notes.explanation: Hydraulic turbines convert potential and kinetic energy of water into rotational mechanical shaft power.
definitions: The speed of a geometrically similar turbine capable of producing unit power under unit head.
notes.example: Selecting Pelton wheels for high-head, low-discharge hydroelectric installations.
exam_points: Pelton turbines are impulse turbines, whereas Francis and Kaplan turbines are reaction turbines.

questions: Classify hydraulic turbines and explain the working of a Pelton wheel turbine with velocity triangles.
Discuss the function of draft tubes in reaction turbines and derive efficiency expressions.

quiz.question: What type of hydraulic turbine is best suited for high head and low water discharge installations?
quiz.explanation: Pelton wheels are impulse turbines specifically designed for high-head hydro power plants.

subjects.name: Heat Transfer
objectives: CO1: Understand modes of heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) and governing equations.
CO2: Solve steady and unsteady conduction problems and analyze extended surfaces (fins).
CO3: Evaluate convective heat transfer coefficients, boiling, condensation, and heat exchanger performance.

syllabus.topics: Conduction: Fourier's law of heat conduction, thermal conductivity, three-dimensional heat conduction equation in Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates. One-dimensional steady-state conduction in composite slabs, cylinders, and spheres, critical radius of insulation.

Extended Surfaces & Transient Conduction: Heat transfer from fins (rectangular and circular profiles), fin efficiency and effectiveness. Lumped capacitance method for transient heat conduction, Biot and Fourier numbers.

Convection & Radiation: Newton's law of cooling, boundary layer theory, forced and natural convection dimensionless numbers (Nusselt, Prandtl, Reynolds, Grashof numbers). Radiation: Thermal radiation, Stefan-Boltzmann law, Planck's law, blackbody radiation, view factors, radiation exchange between gray bodies.
Heat Exchangers: Classification of heat exchangers, LMTD (Logarithmic Mean Temperature Difference) method, effectiveness-NTU method for parallel and counter-flow heat exchangers.

notes.title: Fourier's Law & Critical Radius of Insulation
notes.explanation: Conduction heat transfer is driven by temperature gradients across solid media adhering to Fourier's law.
definitions: The radius of insulation up to which heat transfer increases before decreasing with added insulation thickness for cylinders and spheres.
notes.example: Calculating heat loss through multi-layer composite pipe walls in industrial steam networks.
exam_points: For cylinders, critical radius r_c = k / h, where k is thermal conductivity and h is convective heat transfer coefficient.

questions: State Fourier's law of heat conduction and derive the general heat conduction equation in Cartesian coordinates.
Derive the expression for critical radius of insulation for a cylindrical pipe.

quiz.question: What expression defines the critical radius of insulation for a cylindrical wire or pipe?
quiz.explanation: Critical radius for cylinders is r_c = k / h, maximizing heat transfer when insulation thickness is small.

subjects.name: Design of Machine Elements
objectives: CO1: Apply mechanical engineering design principles, theories of failure, and fatigue criteria.
CO2: Design machine components subjected to static and fluctuating loads (shafts, keys, couplings).
CO3: Design threaded fasteners, welded joints, springs, power screws, and bearings.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Design: Design process, mechanical properties, factor of safety, theories of elastic failure (Maximum shear stress, maximum normal stress, distortion energy theories), stress concentration, fatigue failure, S-N curve, Goodman and Soderberg equations.
Shafts, Keys & Couplings: Design of solid and hollow shafts subjected to torsion, bending, and combined loads. Design of keys, splines, and rigid/flexible shaft couplings.
Fasteners & Joints: Design of threaded fasteners, bolt tightening, eccentric loading on bolted joints. Welded joints: Stresses in fillet and butt welds under eccentric loads.

Springs & Bearings: Helical compression and tension springs, surge in springs. Sliding contact bearings, hydrodynamic lubrication theory, rolling contact ball and roller bearings, load rating and selection.

notes.title: Fatigue Failure & Goodman Diagrams
notes.explanation: Machine components subjected to cyclic fluctuating loads fail at stress levels well below yield strength due to fatigue.
definitions: The maximum alternating stress amplitude that a material can withstand indefinitely without fatigue failure.
notes.example: Designing rotating drive shafts under combined fluctuating bending and torsional stresses using Goodman lines.
exam_points: Goodman criterion provides a conservative linear design relation between mean stress and alternating stress.

questions: Explain theories of elastic failure for ductile and brittle materials.
Discuss stress concentration factors and how to minimize stress concentration in machine parts.

quiz.question: What curve establishes the relationship between alternating stress amplitude and cycles to failure in fatigue testing?
quiz.explanation: The S-N curve plots alternating stress S against number of cycles to failure N.

subjects.name: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning
objectives: CO1: Understand air refrigeration systems and vapor compression refrigeration cycles.
CO2: Analyze vapor absorption systems, refrigerants, and multi-pressure refrigeration systems.
CO3: Master psychrometric principles, comfort air conditioning, and cooling load calculations.

syllabus.topics: Air Refrigeration Systems: Introduction to refrigeration, Carnot refrigeration cycle, Bell-Coleman air refrigeration cycle for aircraft cabins. Vapor Compression Refrigeration (VCR): Standard VCR cycle, P-h and T-s charts, subcooling, superheating, performance COP enhancement.

Multi-Pressure Systems & Absorption Refrigeration: Multistage compression systems with flash intercoolers, cascade refrigeration systems. Vapor absorption refrigeration (VAR) systems: Li-Br and ammonia-water systems, comparison with VCR.

Refrigerants & Equipment: Classification of refrigerants, nomenclature, environmental impact (ODP, GWP), eco-friendly refrigerants. Refrigeration compressors, condensers, evaporators, expansion devices (capillary tube, thermostatic expansion valve).

Air Conditioning & Psychrometry: Psychrometric properties, psychrometric chart processes (sensible heating/cooling, humidification, dehumidification, mixing), effective temperature, human comfort, cooling load estimation basics.

notes.title: Vapor Compression Refrigeration (VCR) Cycle
notes.explanation: The VCR cycle utilizes phase change refrigerant properties to transfer heat from low-temperature reservoirs to high-temperature sinks.
definitions: The ratio of cooling effect produced to the electrical work input required by the compressor.
notes.example: Analyzing household refrigerator cycles using pressure-enthalpy (P-h) property charts.
exam_points: Superheating suction vapor and subcooling liquid condensate improve VCR cycle COP.

questions: Explain the standard vapor compression refrigeration (VCR) cycle with T-s and P-h diagrams.
Discuss aircraft air refrigeration systems (Bell-Coleman cycle).

quiz.question: What performance coefficient parameter evaluates refrigeration systems analogous to thermal efficiency?
quiz.explanation: COP measures the efficiency of refrigeration and heat pump systems.

subjects.name: Automobile Engineering
objectives: CO1: Understand automobile layout, IC engine auxiliary systems, and fuel supply systems.
CO2: Master transmission systems, clutches, gearboxes, propeller shafts, and differential mechanisms.
CO3: Explore suspension systems, steering geometry, braking systems, and electric/hybrid vehicle tech.

syllabus.topics: Introduction & Engine Systems: Automobile classification, layout, chassis frames, engine construction, lubrication and cooling systems, carburetion, MPFI, CRDI diesel fuel injection systems.

Transmission Systems: Clutch types (single plate, multi-plate, centrifugal), manual and automatic gearboxes, fluid couplings, torque converters, propeller shaft, universal joints, differential gear mechanism.

Steering & Suspension Systems: Steering geometry (caster, camber, toe-in, toe-out, kingpin inclination), power steering. Suspension systems: Leaf springs, coil springs, torsion bars, shock absorbers, independent suspension.

Braking Systems & Electric Vehicles: Hydraulic brakes, mechanical brakes, air brakes, ABS (Anti-lock Braking System). Introduction to electric vehicles (EVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), battery management systems.

notes.title: Differential Mechanism in Automobiles
notes.explanation: The differential gear mechanism allows outer drive wheels to rotate faster than inner wheels when rounding vehicle corners.
definitions: A planetary gear train that splits engine torque into two outputs allowing them to spin at different rotational speeds.
notes.example: Calculating outer and inner wheel rotational speeds during vehicle turning maneuvers.
exam_points: Standard open differentials transmit equal torque to both drive wheels regardless of traction differences.

questions: Explain the construction and working of an automobile differential mechanism.
Discuss multi-plate clutches versus single-plate friction clutches.

quiz.question: What gear mechanism allows drive wheels to rotate at unequal speeds when negotiating vehicle turns?
quiz.explanation: The differential enables outer wheels to spin faster than inner wheels during cornering.

subjects.name: Mechanical Vibrations
objectives: CO1: Understand fundamentals of free and forced mechanical vibrations in single degree of freedom systems.
CO2: Analyze damped vibrations, logarithmic decrement, and vibration isolation principles.
CO3: Explore two degree of freedom systems, torsional vibrations, and critical speeds of shafts.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Vibrations: Definitions, simple harmonic motion, free undamped vibrations of single degree of freedom (SDOF) systems, Rayleigh's energy method, equivalent spring stiffness.
Damped Vibrations: Viscous damping, underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped systems, logarithmic decrement, Coulomb damping, structural damping.
Forced Vibrations: SDOF systems subjected to harmonic excitation, magnification factor, phase angle, resonance, vibration isolation, force transmissibility, whirling of shafts and critical speeds.
Multi-Degree of Freedom Systems: Two degree of freedom systems, free vibration of undamped coupled systems, vibration absorbers, torsional vibrations of multi-rotor systems.

notes.title: Logarithmic Decrement & Damping
notes.explanation: Logarithmic decrement measures the rate at which free damped oscillation amplitudes decay over successive cycles.
definitions: The natural logarithm of the ratio of two successive peak vibration amplitudes in free damped systems.
notes.example: Determining damping ratio zeta experimentally from free vibration amplitude decay records.
exam_points: Formula: delta = ln(x_1 / x_2) = (2 * pi * zeta) / sqrt(1 - zeta^2).

questions: Derive the expression for logarithmic decrement in viscously damped free vibration systems.
Explain vibration isolation and transmissibility ratio for harmonically excited machinery.

quiz.question: What parameter measures the rate of decay of free oscillations in viscously damped mechanical systems?
quiz.explanation: Logarithmic decrement quantifies the exponential decay rate of damped free vibration amplitudes.

subjects.name: Automation in Manufacturing
objectives: CO1: Understand automation strategies, manufacturing systems, and automated flow lines.
CO2: Master numerical control (NC), CNC programming, and industrial robotics architecture.
CO3: Explore flexible manufacturing systems (FMS), computer-integrated manufacturing (CIM), and automated inspection.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Automation: Automated manufacturing strategies, fixed, programmable, and flexible automation, automated flow lines, transfer mechanisms, analysis of transfer lines without storage.
Numerical Control (NC) & CNC Systems: Fundamentals of NC, CNC, and DNC machines, axes designation, interpolators, CNC part programming (G and M codes) for turning and milling operations.
Industrial Robotics: Robot anatomy, configurations, coordinate systems, end effectors, sensors, robot programming languages, industrial applications in welding, assembly, and material handling.

Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMS) & CIM: FMS components, workstations, material handling systems, computer-integrated manufacturing (CIM), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), automated inspection (CMM).

notes.title: CNC Part Programming & G-Codes
notes.explanation: CNC part programs utilize standardized G-codes and M-codes to instruct machine tools on toolpaths and spindle speeds.
definitions: Preparatory function codes that direct CNC machine tool movements and interpolation modes (e.g., G01 linear interpolation).
notes.example: Writing CNC turning part programs for contouring cylindrical workpiece components.
exam_points: G00 designates rapid positioning, while G01 specifies controlled linear cutting feed motion.

questions: Explain the differences between NC, CNC, and DNC machine tool architectures.
Write a CNC turning part program incorporating G-codes and M-codes for step turning.

quiz.question: What CNC preparatory code specifies rapid positioning movement without cutting feed?
quiz.explanation: G00 commands rapid traverse positioning of machine tool axes.

subjects.name: Software Training & Industrial Capstone Project
objectives: CO1: Apply cumulative B.Tech Mechanical Engineering knowledge to solve real-world industry design and manufacturing problems.
CO2: Design, prototype, test, and analyze mechanical engineering systems using CAD/CAE software tools.
CO3: Demonstrate professional technical communication, report writing, and project defense proficiency.

syllabus.topics: Industry Internship: Full-time industrial training or mechanical engineering placement in manufacturing plants, thermal power stations, or design studios.
Capstone Project: Design, fabrication, simulation, and testing of an advanced mechanical engineering system or automation assembly.
Project Report & Viva Voce: Preparation of technical documentation, CAD drawings, FEA simulation reports, and final defense presentation.

notes.title: Industrial Mechanical Design & CAE
notes.explanation: Capstone projects bridge academic theory with practical industrial manufacturing and computer-aided engineering simulations.
definitions: A computerized numerical method for predicting how physical structures react to real-world forces, heat, and vibration.
notes.example: Performing stress analysis and CFD flow simulations on mechanical component assemblies using ANSYS or SolidWorks.
exam_points: Rigorous mesh refinement and boundary condition validation ensure accurate FEA simulation results.

questions: Describe the design methodology, manufacturing processes, and CAE analysis results of your capstone mechanical project.
Discuss engineering challenges encountered during prototype fabrication and testing.

quiz.question: What computer-aided engineering method subdivides complex physical domains into discrete geometric elements for stress analysis?
quiz.explanation: FEA discretizes continuous structures into finite elements to solve differential equilibrium equations.

Bachelor of Technology in Electronics &.full_name: Bachelor of Technology in Electronics and Computer Engineering

subjects.name: Mathematics-I (Calculus & Linear Algebra)
objectives: CO1: Apply differential and integral calculus concepts to engineering problems.
CO2: Solve ordinary differential equations of first and higher orders.
CO3: Understand matrices, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and linear transformations.

syllabus.topics: Calculus: Limit, continuity, and differentiability, Rolle's theorem, Mean value theorems, Taylor's and Maclaurin's series. Evaluation of definite and improper integrals.
Multivariable Calculus: Functions of several variables, partial derivatives, total derivative, Euler's theorem, maxima and minima, Jacobian.
Ordinary Differential Equations: First order differential equations, exact equations, linear differential equations of higher order with constant coefficients.
Matrices: Rank of a matrix, elementary transformations, system of linear equations, characteristic equation, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, Cayley-Hamilton theorem.

notes.title: Calculus & Series Expansions
notes.explanation: Calculus forms the foundation for analyzing continuous signals, optimization, and function approximations in electronics engineering.
definitions: A representation of a function as an infinite sum of terms calculated from the values of its derivatives at a single point.
notes.example: Approximating nonlinear electronic device characteristics using Taylor polynomial expansions.
exam_points: Rolle's theorem requires a function to be continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and f(a)=f(b).

notes.title: Matrices & Eigenvalues
notes.explanation: Matrix algebra and eigenvalue analysis are essential for solving state-space equations in control systems and network analysis.
definitions: A scalar lambda associated with a linear system of equations such that Av = lambda*v.
notes.example: Calculating natural frequencies and modal responses for multi-loop circuit networks.
exam_points: The Cayley-Hamilton theorem states that every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation.

questions: State and verify Rolle's theorem for the function f(x) = x^3 - 4x on interval [0,2].
Expand e^x * sin(x) in powers of x using Maclaurin's theorem.
Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the matrix A = [[1, 2], [3, 2]].
Verify Cayley-Hamilton theorem for a given 3x3 matrix and compute its inverse.

quiz.question: What theorem states that if f(x) is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and f(a)=f(b), there exists c such that f'(c)=0?
quiz.explanation: Rolle's theorem guarantees at least one stationary point where the derivative equals zero under those conditions.

quiz.question: What does the Cayley-Hamilton theorem establish for any square matrix A?
options: A satisfies its own characteristic equation
The trace of A equals the sum of its eigenvalues
quiz.explanation: The theorem proves that replacing lambda with matrix A in its characteristic polynomial yields a zero matrix.

subjects.name: Programming for Problem Solving
objectives: CO1: Understand computer hardware, software, and basic algorithmic problem solving.
CO2: Master C programming fundamentals including control structures, arrays, and functions.
CO3: Implement pointers, structures, unions, and file handling operations in C.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Programming: Computer system components, algorithms, flowcharts, pseudo-code. C fundamentals: Data types, operators, input/output statements.
Control Statements & Arrays: Conditional branching (if, switch), loops (while, for, do-while), 1D and 2D arrays, character strings and string manipulation functions.
Functions & Pointers: Function declaration, definition, recursion, parameter passing by value and reference. Pointers: Pointer arithmetic, dynamic memory allocation.
Structures, Unions & File Handling: User-defined data types, structures, arrays of structures, unions, file I/O operations.

notes.title: Pointers & Dynamic Memory
notes.explanation: Pointers store memory addresses, enabling efficient array traversal and dynamic memory allocation in embedded firmware development.
definitions: A variable whose value is the address of another location in computer memory.
notes.example: Using malloc() and free() to allocate dynamic memory buffers in C programs.
exam_points: Passing arguments by reference allows functions to modify original caller variables directly.

questions: Explain call by value versus call by reference in C functions with code examples.
Discuss dynamic memory allocation functions (malloc, calloc, realloc, free) in C.

quiz.question: Which operator is used to access the memory address of a variable in C?
quiz.explanation: The address-of operator (&) returns the memory address of a variable.

subjects.name: Basic Electrical Engineering
objectives: CO1: Analyze DC and AC electrical circuits using network theorems.
CO2: Understand magnetic circuits, single-phase, and three-phase AC systems.
CO3: Explore electrical machines, transformers, and electrical installations.

syllabus.topics: DC Circuits: Electrical circuit elements (R, L, C), voltage and current sources, Kirchhoff's laws, mesh and nodal analysis, network theorems (Superposition, Thevenin's, Norton's, Maximum Power Transfer).
AC Circuits: Representation of sinusoidal waveforms, peak and RMS values, phasor representation, real, reactive, and apparent power, power factor, series and parallel RLC circuits, resonance.
Three Phase Systems & Magnetic Circuits: Three-phase balanced circuits, star and delta connections, line and phase quantities, magnetic circuits, reluctance, B-H curve, electromagnetic induction.

Electrical Machines & Transformers: Single-phase transformer construction, EMF equation, equivalent circuit, losses and efficiency. Introduction to DC machines, induction motors, and synchronous generators.

notes.title: Thevenin's Theorem
notes.explanation: Thevenin's theorem simplifies linear active networks into a single equivalent voltage source in series with an impedance.
definitions: The open-circuit voltage measured across load terminals of an electrical network.
notes.example: Replacing complex biasing resistor networks in transistor amplifier circuits with Thevenin equivalents.
exam_points: To find Thevenin resistance, deactivate all independent voltage sources (short circuit) and current sources (open circuit).

questions: State and prove Thevenin's theorem with an illustrative DC circuit example.
Explain Maximum Power Transfer theorem for DC and AC networks.

quiz.question: How are independent voltage sources treated when finding Thevenin equivalent resistance in a linear circuit?
options: Replaced by a constant current source
quiz.explanation: Independent voltage sources are short-circuited (zero internal impedance) when calculating equivalent resistance.

subjects.name: Mathematics-II (Differential Equations & Numerical Methods)
objectives: CO1: Solve linear differential equations using Laplace transforms.
CO2: Apply vector calculus including gradient, divergence, curl, and integral theorems.
CO3: Solve algebraic, transcendental, and differential equations using numerical methods.

syllabus.topics: Laplace Transforms: Definition, properties, evaluation of integrals by Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transforms, convolution theorem, solution of ordinary differential equations.
Vector Calculus: Gradient, divergence, and curl, vector identities, line, surface, and volume integrals, Green's, Gauss's, and Stokes' theorems.
Numerical Methods-I: Solution of algebraic and transcendental equations (Bisection, Regula-Falsi, Newton-Raphson methods), finite differences, interpolation.
Numerical Methods-II: Numerical differentiation and integration, numerical solution of ordinary differential equations (Euler's, Runge-Kutta methods).

notes.title: Laplace Transforms
notes.explanation: Laplace transforms convert linear differential equations into algebraic equations, simplifying transient circuit analysis.
definitions: An integral transform converting a function of time t to a function of complex frequency s.
notes.example: Solving RC and RL transient circuit differential equations using Laplace transform tables.
exam_points: The convolution theorem evaluates inverse transforms of products of transformed functions.

questions: Find the Laplace transform of t^2 * e^(-3t) sin(2t).
State and prove the convolution theorem for Laplace transforms.

quiz.question: What is the Laplace transform of the unit step function u(t-a)?
quiz.explanation: The Laplace transform of u(t-a) is e^(-as)/s by the shifting property.

subjects.name: Analog Electronics
objectives: CO1: Understand semiconductor diode characteristics, rectifiers, and wave shaping circuits.
CO2: Master BJT and MOSFET biasing, small-signal equivalent circuits, and amplifier analysis.
CO3: Explore operational amplifiers, feedback amplifiers, and sinusoidal oscillators.

syllabus.topics: Semiconductor Diodes: P-N junction diode, VI characteristics, diode models, rectifiers (half-wave, full-wave, bridge), filters, Zener diode voltage regulators, clipping and clamping circuits.
Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJT): BJT configurations (CB, CE, CC), operating regions, DC biasing, load line analysis, thermal runaway, hybrid-pi model, small-signal amplifiers.
Field Effect Transistors (FETs): JFET characteristics, pinch-off voltage, MOSFET (enhancement and depletion types), biasing circuits, MOSFET amplifiers.

Operational Amplifiers & Oscillators: Ideal op-amp characteristics, inverting and non-inverting amplifiers, summing amplifier, integrator, differentiator, Barkhausen criterion, RC phase shift and Wien bridge oscillators.

notes.title: Zener Diode Voltage Regulation
notes.explanation: Zener diodes operate in the breakdown region to maintain a nearly constant DC output voltage across varying load currents.
definitions: Reverse breakdown caused by quantum tunneling of electrons across narrow depletion regions in heavily doped p-n junctions.
notes.example: Designing shunt voltage regulator circuits to stabilize DC power supply rails against input voltage fluctuations.
exam_points: Zener regulators require series resistors to limit diode current below maximum power dissipation ratings.

questions: Explain the VI characteristics of a Zener diode and its operation as a voltage regulator.
Compare full-wave center-tapped rectifier and bridge rectifier efficiency and ripple factor.

quiz.question: What region of operation enables Zener diodes to function as stable voltage regulators?
quiz.explanation: Zener diodes operate in reverse breakdown where voltage remains nearly constant over a wide current range.

subjects.name: Data Structure & Algorithms
objectives: CO1: Analyze performance of algorithms using asymptotic notations and time-space trade-offs.
CO2: Implement linear and non-linear data structures including stacks, queues, linked lists, and trees.
CO3: Apply sorting, hashing, and graph traversal algorithms to solve computational problems.

syllabus.topics: Introduction: Elementary data organizations, data structure operations, algorithm analysis, asymptotic notations, time-space trade-off. Searching: Linear search, binary search, complexity analysis.
Stacks and Queues: ADT stack operations, expression conversion and evaluation. ADT queue types: Simple queue, circular queue, priority queue, operations and algorithms.
Linked Lists and Trees: Singly, doubly, and circular linked lists. Tree terminology, binary trees, binary search trees, AVL trees, B-trees, and B+ trees.
Sorting and Hashing: Selection sort, bubble sort, insertion sort, quick sort, merge sort, heap sort, performance comparison, and hashing.
Graph: Basic terminologies, representations, graph search, and traversal algorithms with complexity analysis.

notes.title: Asymptotic Analysis & Searching
notes.explanation: Algorithm efficiency is evaluated using asymptotic notations to measure growth rates of time and space requirements.
definitions: A mathematical notation describing the upper bound of an algorithm's running time complexity.
notes.example: Comparing linear search (O(n)) and binary search (O(log n)) search times on sorted arrays.
exam_points: Binary search requires a pre-sorted array and divides the search space in half during each iteration.

questions: Define asymptotic notations and analyze the time complexity of binary search.
Compare linear search and binary search algorithms with respect to input size.

quiz.question: What data structure operational principle characterizes a Stack?
quiz.explanation: Stacks operate on LIFO principles where the last element inserted is the first one removed.

subjects.name: Digital Electronics
objectives: CO1: Understand number systems, boolean algebra, logic gates, and Karnaugh map minimization.
CO2: Design combinational logic circuits (adders, multiplexers, decoders, comparators).
CO3: Master sequential logic circuits (flip-flops, registers, counters, finite state machines).

syllabus.topics: Number Systems & Boolean Algebra: Binary, octal, hexadecimal number systems, base conversions, binary codes, logic gates, Boolean postulates, De Morgan's theorems, SOP and POS canonical forms, K-map minimization.
Combinational Logic Circuits: Half adder, full adder, binary subtractor, multiplexers, demultiplexers, encoders, decoders, code converters, magnitude comparators, parity generators.

Sequential Logic Circuits: Latches, flip-flops (SR, JK, D, T, Master-Slave), triggering methods, race around condition, shift registers (SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO), ripple counters, synchronous counters.
Memory Devices & Logic Families: Semiconductor memories (RAM, ROM, EEPROM), programmable logic devices (PAL, PLA, FPGA introduction), logic families (TTL, CMOS electrical characteristics).

notes.title: Karnaugh Map Minimization
notes.explanation: K-maps provide a systematic graphical method for simplifying Boolean expressions into minimal sum-of-products forms.
definitions: A product term in a Boolean expression that covers one or more minterms of a function.
notes.example: Simplifying a 4-variable Boolean expression by grouping adjacent cells of 1s in K-maps.
exam_points: Essential prime implicants must be included in minimal sum-of-products cover solutions.

questions: Simplify the Boolean function F(A,B,C,D) = sum(0,2,5,7,8,10,13,15) using Karnaugh maps.
Explain universal logic gates (NAND and NOR) and realize basic gates using them.

quiz.question: Which logic gates are universally capable of implementing any Boolean logic function?
quiz.explanation: NAND and NOR gates are universal gates because any combinational logic circuit can be built using only NAND or only NOR gates.

subjects.name: Computer Architecture & Organization
objectives: CO1: Understand computer system structure, instruction formats, and addressing modes.
CO2: Master CPU design, hardwired/microprogrammed control units, and arithmetic algorithms.
CO3: Explore memory hierarchy, cache management, virtual memory, and I/O interfacing.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Computer Organization: Functional units, register transfer language, bus and memory transfers, arithmetic, logic, and shift micro-operations, instruction codes, computer registers, instruction cycle, addressing modes.

Central Processing Unit & Control Unit: General register organization, stack organization, instruction formats, data transfer and manipulation, program control. Control unit: Hardwired control, microprogrammed control.

Computer Arithmetic & Memory Organization: Addition and subtraction algorithms, Booth's multiplication algorithm, division algorithms. Memory hierarchy, primary memory, auxiliary memory, associative memory, cache memory mapping techniques, virtual memory.
Input-Output Organization: Peripheral devices, I/O interface, modes of transfer (programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O, Direct Memory Access), pipelining and vector processing introduction.

notes.title: Booth's Multiplication Algorithm
notes.explanation: Booth's algorithm multiplies signed binary integers in two's complement representation efficiently by examining adjacent pairs of bits.
definitions: A grouping technique in Booth's algorithm examining multiplier bits (bi, bi-1) to determine addition, subtraction, or shifting operations.
notes.example: Multiplying signed numbers +3 and -4 using 4-bit Booth's algorithm registers.
exam_points: Strings of 0s or 1s in the multiplier are handled with fast shifting steps, reducing addition cycles.

questions: Explain Booth's multiplication algorithm and multiply (-5) by (+3) using 5-bit registers.
Discuss cache memory mapping techniques (Direct, Associative, and Set-Associative mapping).

quiz.question: What algorithm efficiently multiplies signed two's complement binary numbers?
quiz.explanation: Booth's algorithm handles signed two's complement multiplication by examining bit pairs.

subjects.name: Microprocessors & Microcontrollers
objectives: CO1: Understand 8086 microprocessor architecture, pin diagram, bus organization, and assembly language programming.
CO2: Master interrupt structures, memory interfacing, and I/O peripheral chips (8255, 8253, 8259).
CO3: Explore 8051 microcontroller architecture, instruction set, timers, serial communication, and interfacing.

syllabus.topics: 8086 Microprocessor Architecture: 8086 architecture, EU and BIU, register organization, pin description, physical address generation, bus cycle, minimum and maximum modes, assembly language programming instructions.
Interfacing & Peripheral ICs: Memory interfacing, RAM and ROM chips. Programmable peripheral interface 8255 PPI, programmable interval timer 8253, programmable interrupt controller 8259, USART 8251.

8051 Microcontroller Architecture: Introduction to 8051 microcontroller, architecture, pin diagram, internal RAM and ROM organization, special function registers, ports, timer/counters, serial communication.
8051 Programming & Interfacing: 8051 instruction set, addressing modes, assembly programming. Interfacing external memory, keyboards, 7-segment displays, ADC, DAC, and stepper motors with 8051.

notes.title: 8086 Physical Address Generation
notes.explanation: The 8086 BIU generates 20-bit physical addresses by shifting a 16-bit segment register left by 4 bits and adding a 16-bit offset.
definitions: A 16-bit register (CS, DS, SS, ES) storing base memory addresses for code, data, stack, and extra segments.
notes.example: Calculating physical address for Segment = `0x1000` and Offset = `0x0045` yielding `0x10045`.
exam_points: Formula: Physical Address = (Segment Register * 16) + Offset.

questions: Explain the internal architecture of 8086 microprocessor with a block diagram emphasizing EU and BIU.
Describe physical address generation in 8086 with an illustrative numerical example.

quiz.question: How many bits wide is the physical address bus in the 8086 microprocessor?
quiz.explanation: The 8086 has a 20-bit address bus, enabling direct access to 1 MB of physical memory space (2^20 bytes).

subjects.name: Linear Integrated Circuits
objectives: CO1: Understand differential amplifier configurations, current mirrors, and op-amp internal circuitry.
CO2: Master linear and non-linear op-amp applications, active filters, and oscillators.
CO3: Explore specialized ICs including 555 timers, Phase Locked Loops (PLL), and voltage regulators.

syllabus.topics: Differential Amplifiers & Op-Amp Fundamentals: Differential amplifier configurations, dual-input balanced-output, current mirror circuits, IC op-amp block diagram, parameters (CMRR, slew rate, input offset voltage), open-loop and closed-loop configurations.

Linear & Non-Linear Op-Amp Applications: Inverting and non-inverting amplifiers, voltage follower, summing amplifier, instrumentation amplifier, V-to-I and I-to-V converters, comparators, Schmitt trigger, precision rectifiers, log and antilog amplifiers.

Active Filters & Waveform Generators: Butterworth active filters (First and second order low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-stop filters). Oscillators: Phase shift, Wien bridge, square wave, triangular wave, and sawtooth generators.

Specialized ICs: 555 Timer IC (monostable and astable multivibrator modes), Phase Locked Loop (PLL) IC 565, voltage regulator ICs (78xx, 79xx, LM317 adjustable regulators), switched-mode power supplies (SMPS).

notes.title: 555 Timer Astable Multivibrator
notes.explanation: The 555 timer connected in astable mode functions as a free-running relaxation oscillator producing continuous clock pulses.
definitions: The ratio of high pulse duration to total signal period in a square wave waveform.
notes.example: Calculating oscillation frequency $f = 1.44 / ((R_1 + 2R_2)C)$ for astable 555 timer circuits.
exam_points: Charging time depends on $(R_1 + R_2)C$ while discharging depends on $R_2C$.

questions: Explain the internal architecture and working of 555 Timer IC operating in astable mode.
Discuss second-order Butterworth low-pass active filter design using operational amplifiers.

quiz.question: What formula calculates the oscillation frequency of a 555 timer astable multivibrator?
quiz.explanation: The oscillation frequency for astable 555 timers is given by $f = 1.44 / ((R_1 + 2R_2)C)$.

subjects.name: Database Management Systems
objectives: CO1: Understand relational database models, ER modeling, and relational algebra.
CO2: Master SQL queries, integrity constraints, and database normalization (1NF to BCNF).
CO3: Explore transaction management, concurrency control, and recovery systems.

syllabus.topics: Introduction: Database system architecture, ER model, entities, attributes, relationship sets. Relational Model: Relational algebra.
Structured Query Language (SQL): DDL, DML, DCL, basic queries, nested queries, joins, views, aggregate functions, integrity constraints, triggers.
Relational Database Design: Functional dependencies, Armstrong's axioms, closure of attributes, normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF), lossless decomposition.
Transactions & Concurrency Control: ACID properties, transaction states, schedules, serializability, lock-based protocols (2PL), timestamp-based protocols.

notes.title: Database Normalization
notes.explanation: Normalization eliminates data redundancy and insertion/deletion anomalies by decomposing relations into higher normal forms.
definitions: A stricter version of 3NF requiring that for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey.
notes.example: Decomposing an unnormalized relation violating 2NF into relations with fully functional dependencies.
exam_points: Lossless join decomposition ensures no spurious tuples are generated when joining decomposed relations.

questions: Define functional dependency and explain normalization up to BCNF with examples.
Discuss Armstrong's axioms and the computation of attribute set closures.

quiz.question: What property ensures that database transactions execute reliably adhering to Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability?
quiz.explanation: ACID properties guarantee reliable transaction processing in database management systems.

subjects.name: Computer Networks
objectives: CO1: Understand OSI and TCP/IP reference models, physical layer data transmission, and analog/digital modulation.
CO2: Master data link layer protocols, error detection/correction, MAC sublayer, and LAN architectures.
CO3: Explore network layer routing protocols, transport layer reliable transmission (TCP/UDP), and application layer services.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Computer Networks: OSI and TCP/IP models, physical layer, transmission media, multiplexing, circuit switching, packet switching, data and signal impairments.
Data Link Layer: Framing, error detection and correction (Hamming code, CRC), sliding window protocols, Medium Access Control (MAC), ALOHA, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA, Ethernet IEEE 802.3, wireless LANs.

Network Layer: Network layer design issues, routing algorithms (Distance Vector, Link State), congestion control algorithms, IPv4 addressing, subnetting, CIDR, IPv6, NAT, routing protocols (RIP, OSPF, BGP).

Transport & Application Layers: Transport layer services, UDP, TCP reliable data transfer, flow control, congestion control, TCP connection establishment (3-way handshake). Application layer: DNS, SMTP, HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, DHCP.

notes.title: TCP 3-Way Handshake
notes.explanation: The TCP three-way handshake establishes a reliable connection between client and server before data transmission begins.
definitions: A synchronization control packet sent by a client to initiate a network connection request.
notes.example: Sequence of exchange: Client sends SYN -> Server responds with SYN-ACK -> Client replies with ACK.
exam_points: Sequence numbers are initialized during the handshake to guarantee ordered packet delivery.

questions: Explain the TCP connection establishment 3-way handshake process with state transition diagrams.
Compare IPv4 and IPv6 header structures and address formats.

quiz.question: What control packet sequence establishes a TCP connection in computer networks?
quiz.explanation: TCP connections are established using the SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK packet exchange sequence.

subjects.name: VLSI Design
objectives: CO1: Understand MOS transistor physics, fabrication processes, and CMOS inverter characteristics.
CO2: Master stick diagrams, layout design rules, combinational and sequential CMOS logic design.
CO3: Explore semiconductor memories, FPGA architectures, and VLSI testing methodologies.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to MOSFETs & Fabrication: Evolution of ICs, MOS transistor threshold voltage, VI characteristics, CMOS fabrication process steps (n-well, p-well, twin-tub), layout design rules.
CMOS Inverter & Characteristics: CMOS inverter DC characteristics, static and dynamic power dissipation, noise margin, propagation delay, sizing and optimization of CMOS inverters.
CMOS Logic Circuit Design: Combinational CMOS logic circuits, pass transistor logic, transmission gates, dynamic CMOS logic, sequential CMOS circuits (latches, flip-flops, registers).
Semiconductor Memories & FPGA: SRAM, DRAM cell architectures, read/write circuitry. Programmable logic devices, CPLDs, FPGA architecture and interconnects, VLSI testing and DFT.

notes.title: CMOS Inverter Noise Margin
notes.explanation: Noise margins define the noise immunity of CMOS logic gates operating in digital systems.
definitions: The difference between maximum low input voltage recognized by a gate and maximum low output voltage generated ($V_{IL} - V_{OL}$).
notes.example: Calculating $N_ML$ and $N_MH$ for CMOS inverters operating at 3.3V supply voltages.
exam_points: Higher noise margins ensure robust digital signal transmission across interconnected VLSI chips.

questions: Derive the expression for threshold voltage and DC transfer characteristics of a CMOS inverter.
Discuss static and dynamic power dissipation sources in CMOS integrated circuits.

quiz.question: What parameter defines the ability of a CMOS logic gate to tolerate noise on its input terminals?
quiz.explanation: Noise margins quantify the maximum noise voltage superimposed on input signals without causing false gate switching.

subjects.name: Embedded Systems
objectives: CO1: Understand embedded system architecture, hardware/software co-design, and real-time operating systems (RTOS).
CO2: Master ARM Cortex-M microcontroller architecture, instruction set, and peripheral programming.
CO3: Explore communication interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART, CAN) and IoT embedded application development.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Embedded Systems: Characteristics, hardware and software architecture, embedded processors, memory selection, sensors and actuators interfacing, design life cycle.
ARM Cortex-M Architecture: ARM architecture evolution, ARM Cortex-M processor registers, exception and interrupt handling, nested vectored interrupt controller (NVIC), assembly and C programming.
Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS): Operating system basics, tasks, task states, processes and threads, context switching, semaphore, mutex, message queues, priority inversion, scheduling algorithms.
Communication Interfaces & Applications: Serial communication protocols (UART, SPI, I2C, CAN bus, USB), wireless protocols (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/BLE), case studies in automotive and IoT embedded systems.

notes.title: I2C Communication Protocol
notes.explanation: I2C is a synchronous, multi-master, multi-slave, packet-switched serial communication bus utilizing two bidirectional lines.
definitions: Serial Data Line (SDA) and Serial Clock Line (SCL) comprising the physical I2C bus wiring.
notes.example: Interfacing digital temperature sensors and EEPROM memory chips to microcontrollers using I2C addresses.
exam_points: I2C devices are identified by unique 7-bit or 10-bit device addresses transmitted over the bus.

questions: Explain the physical layer and protocol frame format of I2C communication bus.
Compare SPI and I2C communication protocols with respect to speed, wiring, and master-slave configurations.

quiz.question: What two signal lines constitute the physical hardware bus in I2C communication?
quiz.explanation: I2C uses two bidirectional open-drain lines: SDA for data and SCL for clock synchronization.

subjects.name: Compiler Design
objectives: CO1: Understand phases of compilation, lexical analysis, regular expressions, and finite automata.
CO2: Master parsing techniques including top-down (LL(1)) and bottom-up (LR, LALR) parsers.
CO3: Explore syntax-directed translation, intermediate code generation, and code optimization.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Compilers: Phases of compilation, compiler construction tools. Lexical Analysis: Role of lexical analyzer, tokens, regular expressions, finite automata.
Syntax Analysis: Role of parser, context-free grammars, parse trees. Top-down parsing: LL(1) grammars. Bottom-up parsing: Shift-reduce parsing, SLR, CLR, and LALR parsers.
Syntax-Directed Translation & Intermediate Code: Syntax-directed definitions, evaluation orders, intermediate languages (three-address code, quadruples, triples).
Run-Time Environments & Code Optimization: Storage organization, activation records. Code Optimization: Principal sources of optimization, basic blocks, code generation.

notes.title: Syntax Analysis & Parsing
notes.explanation: Parsers validate token streams against grammar rules, constructing parse trees for semantic analysis.
definitions: A top-down parser that parses input from Left to right, constructs a Leftmost derivation, using 1 lookahead token.
notes.example: Constructing FIRST and FOLLOW sets to build predictive parsing tables for LL(1) grammars.
exam_points: LR parsers are more powerful than LL parsers and handle bottom-up shift-reduce parsing efficiently.

questions: Explain the construction of FIRST and FOLLOW sets for a given context-free grammar.
Differentiate between LL(1) top-down parsing and LR bottom-up parsing.

quiz.question: What parsing table construction method is used for bottom-up LALR parsers?
quiz.explanation: LALR parsers merge LR(1) states having identical LR(0) items and different lookaheads to reduce table size.

subjects.name: Semester Industrial Training / Electronics & Computer Capstone Project
objectives: CO1: Apply cumulative B.Tech Electronics and Computer Engineering knowledge to solve real-world industry hardware-software integration problems.
CO2: Design, prototype, test, and deploy embedded systems, IoT devices, or VLSI/computer architecture solutions.
CO3: Demonstrate technical documentation, code repositories, and project defense proficiency.

syllabus.topics: Industry Internship: Full-time industrial training or hardware-software engineering placement in approved electronics or IT organizations.
Capstone Project: Design, development, prototyping, and testing of an advanced electronics and computer engineering integrated system.
Project Report & Viva Voce: Preparation of technical documentation, GitHub code repositories, hardware schematics, PCB layouts, and final defense presentation.

notes.title: Industrial Hardware-Software Co-Design
notes.explanation: Capstone projects bridge academic theory with practical industrial embedded hardware design and software application deployment.
definitions: The concurrent design of hardware and software components of a system to meet performance and functional constraints.
notes.example: Developing custom PCB sensor nodes running RTOS firmware interfaced with cloud dashboard servers.
exam_points: Rigorous testing, schematic verification, and modular firmware structuring ensure production reliability.

questions: Describe the hardware architecture, firmware implementation, and system integration details of your capstone project.
Discuss technical challenges encountered during hardware prototyping, debugging, and testing.

quiz.question: What engineering approach concurrently designs electronic hardware and embedded software to optimize system performance?
quiz.explanation: Co-design integrates hardware and software development phases simultaneously for embedded systems.

aliases: semester industrial training / electronics & computer capstone project

M.Tech. CSE.full_name: Master of Technology in Computer Science & Engineering (M.Tech. CSE)

subjects.name: Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science
objectives: CO1: Understand mathematical fundamentals prerequisites for machine learning, data mining, and computer security.
CO2: Develop statistical inference and probabilistic modeling skills.
CO3: Apply graph theory and combinatorics to solve complex computer science problems.

syllabus.topics: Probability mass, density, and cumulative distribution functions, parametric families of distributions, expected value, variance, conditional expectation, univariate and multivariate Central Limit Theorem, probabilistic inequalities, Markov chains.
Random samples, sampling distributions of estimators, Methods of Moments and Maximum Likelihood Estimation.
Statistical inference, multivariate statistical models, regression and classification problems, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), overfitting and model assessment.

Graph Theory: Isomorphism, planar graphs, graph coloring, Hamilton circuits and Euler cycles. Permutations and Combinations with and without repetition, specialized combinatorial enumeration techniques.
Computer science and engineering applications: Data mining, network protocols, web traffic analysis, computer security, software engineering, distributed systems, and machine learning.

notes.title: Probability & Markov Chains
notes.explanation: Probability distributions and Markov chains model stochastic systems and randomized algorithms in computer science.
definitions: A stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events in which the probability of each event depends only on the state attained in the previous event.
notes.example: Modeling web page browsing transitions using discrete-time Markov chains.
exam_points: The Central Limit Theorem states that the distribution of sample means approximates a normal distribution as sample size grows large.

questions: State and explain the univariate Central Limit Theorem and its applications in computing.
Discuss properties of probability mass functions and parametric distribution families.

quiz.question: What stochastic property characterizes a Markov chain?
options: Future states depend on all past history
The memoryless property where next state depends only on the current state
quiz.explanation: Markov chains exhibit the memoryless property where transition probabilities depend solely on the current state.

subjects.name: Advanced Data Structures
objectives: CO1: Choose and implement advanced data structures and dictionaries for efficient algorithmic solutions.
CO2: Master balanced search trees, skip lists, and hashing collision resolution techniques.
CO3: Apply string matching algorithms and computational geometry data structures.

syllabus.topics: Dictionaries: Definition, dictionary ADT, implementation. Hashing: Review of hashing, hash functions, collision resolution techniques (separate chaining, open addressing, linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing, rehashing, extendible hashing).
Skip Lists: Need for randomized data structures, search and update operations on skip lists, probabilistic analysis, deterministic skip lists.
Trees: Binary search trees, AVL trees, Red-Black trees, 2-3 trees, B-trees, Splay trees.

Text Processing: String operations, brute-force pattern matching, Boyer-Moore algorithm, Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) algorithm, standard tries, compressed tries, suffix tries, Huffman coding, Longest Common Subsequence (LCS).
Computational Geometry: One-dimensional and two-dimensional range searching, priority search trees, quadtrees, k-D trees.

notes.title: Red-Black Trees & B-Trees
notes.explanation: Self-balancing search trees guarantee logarithmic time complexity for search, insertion, and deletion operations.
definitions: A binary search tree with extra bit color (red or black) per node ensuring the tree remains balanced during insertions and deletions.
notes.example: Maintaining balanced indexing structures in database storage engines using B-trees.
exam_points: Every path from a node to its descendant NULL leaves must contain the same number of black nodes in Red-Black trees.

questions: Explain the properties of Red-Black trees and illustrate insertion and rotation operations.
Compare AVL trees and B-trees regarding disk access efficiency.

quiz.question: What is the worst-case time complexity for search operations in a balanced Red-Black tree with n nodes?
quiz.explanation: Self-balancing binary search trees like Red-Black trees guarantee O(log n) search, insertion, and deletion times.

subjects.name: Advanced Algorithms
objectives: CO1: Master advanced algorithm design paradigms including matroids, network flow, and randomized algorithms.
CO2: Analyze graph algorithms, shortest paths, and max-flow min-cut theorem.
CO3: Apply discrete Fourier transforms and polynomial arithmetic algorithms.

syllabus.topics: Sorting review, graph definitions, BFS shortest paths, Dijkstra's algorithm, DFS and strongly connected components, amortized analysis.
Matroids: Greedy paradigm, maximum weight independent set, Minimum Spanning Trees. Graph matching: maximum matching, augmenting paths, Edmonds' Blossom algorithm.
Flow-Networks: Max-flow min-cut theorem, Ford-Fulkerson method, Edmonds-Karp algorithm. Matrix computations: Strassen's algorithm, LUP-decomposition.
Shortest Path in Graphs: Floyd-Warshall algorithm. Modular representation of integers/polynomials, Chinese Remainder Theorem, Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT).

notes.title: Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
notes.explanation: The max-flow min-cut theorem states that in a flow network, the maximum flow from source to sink equals the minimum capacity of a cut separating them.
definitions: A graph representing how much additional flow is possible across edges in flow networks.
notes.example: Solving transportation bottleneck and bipartite matching problems using Ford-Fulkerson max-flow algorithms.
exam_points: Edmonds-Karp algorithm uses BFS to find augmenting paths, guaranteeing polynomial time complexity O(V * E^2).

questions: State and prove the Max-Flow Min-Cut theorem in flow networks.
Explain Edmonds-Karp algorithm and compare its time complexity with Ford-Fulkerson method.

quiz.question: What theorem equates the maximum flow in a flow network to the capacity of the minimum cut?
quiz.explanation: The Max-Flow Min-Cut theorem establishes exact duality between maximum flow and minimum cut capacities.

subjects.name: Dissertation-I & Industry Training
objectives: CO1: Undertake original research and literature review in cutting-edge computer science domains.
CO2: Formulate research problems, design methodologies, and implement software prototypes.
CO3: Prepare technical dissertation reports and defend research findings.

Summer Industry Training (6-8 weeks) in reputed IT industries, research laboratories, or academic institutions.
Implementation, initial experimentation, progress evaluation, dissertation report drafting, and seminar presentation.

notes.title: Research Methodology & Problem Formulation
notes.explanation: Rigorous literature reviews identify research gaps, establishing novel contributions in computer science domains.
definitions: An unexplored question or missing perspective identified in existing scholarly literature.
notes.example: Formulating novel machine learning architectures to optimize distributed edge computing latency.
exam_points: Clear problem statements and reproducible experimental evaluations are essential for successful M.Tech dissertations.

questions: Describe the research methodology, literature review findings, and proposed architecture for your dissertation.
Discuss evaluation metrics and experimental benchmarks used in your research study.

quiz.question: What document summarizes initial research progress, literature surveys, and problem formulations for M.Tech evaluation?
quiz.explanation: Dissertation-I documents literature surveys, problem formulation, and preliminary implementation progress.

subjects.name: Dissertation-II (Thesis)
objectives: CO1: Execute complete research investigations, software implementation, and empirical evaluations.
CO2: Analyze experimental results against state-of-the-art benchmarks and draw scientific conclusions.
CO3: Author peer-reviewed research papers and defend thesis findings before expert panels.

syllabus.topics: Full-scale implementation, algorithm tuning, dataset collection, and experimental performance evaluation.
Comparative analysis, ablation studies, result validation, and preparation of research manuscripts for publication.
Final thesis writing, formatting according to university guidelines, open defense, and viva voce examination.

notes.title: Empirical Evaluation & Thesis Defense
notes.explanation: Rigorous experimentation and peer-reviewed validation substantiate scientific contributions in Master's theses.
definitions: An experiment removing feature components to evaluate their individual contributions to system performance.
notes.example: Benchmarking proposed machine learning classification accuracy against baseline algorithms.
exam_points: Thesis defense evaluations assess research originality, technical rigor, and clarity of presentation.

questions: Present the experimental results, performance comparisons, and conclusions derived from your thesis research.
Discuss potential future work and practical industrial applications arising from your study.

quiz.question: What experimental analysis removes individual system components to measure their specific impact?
quiz.explanation: Ablation studies systematically remove components to isolate their contribution to system efficacy.

Explain Edmonds-Karp algorithm and its efficiency.

quiz.question: What theorem establishes duality between maximum flow and minimum cut capacities in networks?

quiz.question: What final examination validates the complete research work and thesis findings of an M.Tech student?
