M.Tech. ME.full_name: Master of Technology in Mechanical Engineering (M.Tech. ME)

subjects.name: Advanced Engineering Materials
objectives: CO1: Understand classification, properties, and selection criteria of advanced engineering materials.
CO2: Master composite materials, ceramic biomaterials, and high/low temperature alloys.
CO3: Explore smart materials, shape memory alloys, and nanomaterials.

syllabus.topics: Classification and Selection of Materials: Classification, required properties, material selection criteria, requirements of advanced materials.
Composite Materials: Fiber reinforced, laminated, and dispersed materials with metallic matrices (Al, Cu, Ti) and non-metallic matrices (polyesters, epoxy resins). Properties and applications.
Ceramics and Glasses: Bio-ceramics, inert ceramics, bio-reactive glasses, porous ceramics, calcium phosphate ceramics, physico-chemical surface modifications.

Low & High Temperature Materials: Cryogenic properties and materials. Superalloys and high-temperature refractory materials. Smart Materials: Shape memory alloys, varistors, intelligent biomedical materials.
Nanomaterials: Definition, types including carbon nanotubes and nanocomposites, physical/mechanical properties, and engineering applications.

notes.title: Composite Materials & Matrix Systems
notes.explanation: Composite materials combine high-strength reinforcing fibers with compliant matrix binders to achieve superior specific strength and stiffness.
definitions: The ratio of a material's tensile strength to its density, critical for aerospace structural design.
notes.example: Utilizing carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites in lightweight aerospace fuselage panels.
exam_points: Matrix phases transfer loads to reinforcing fibers and protect them from environmental degradation.

questions: Classify composite materials and explain the role of metallic and non-metallic matrices.
Discuss shape memory alloys and their intelligent biomedical applications.

quiz.question: What property ratio defines specific strength in advanced engineering materials?
quiz.explanation: Specific strength evaluates strength-to-weight performance ratios crucial for structural weight reduction.

subjects.name: Finite Element Analysis
objectives: CO1: Understand mathematical formulations, weighted residual approaches, and weak boundary value problems.
CO2: Master finite element discretization, shape functions, isoparametric elements, and structural mechanics applications.
CO3: Apply FEM to heat transfer and fluid mechanics differential problems.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to FEM: Basic concepts, historical background, engineering applications, comparison with analytical methods. Formulations: Weighted residual forms, Rayleigh-Ritz method, weak formulation.

Finite Element Techniques: Discretization, element shapes, node locations, interpolation functions, derivation of element equations, convergence criteria, isoparametric elements, Lagrange and Hermite polynomials.
Structural Mechanics: Equilibrium equations, stress-strain relations, plane stress/strain, axisymmetric and 3D problems, analysis of trusses, frames, and solids of revolution.

Heat Transfer & Fluid Mechanics: Variational and Galerkin approaches for 1D/2D steady-state conduction, convection, and radiation. Incompressible viscous flows, stream function-vorticity formulations.

notes.title: Isoparametric Elements & Shape Functions
notes.explanation: Isoparametric elements use the same interpolation functions for defining both geometry and field variables.
definitions: A mathematical interpolation function expressing field variables across elements in terms of nodal values.
notes.example: Mapping arbitrary quadrilateral physical elements onto regular master square elements using natural coordinates.
exam_points: Completeness and compatibility requirements ensure FEM convergence to exact elasticity solutions.

questions: Explain the Rayleigh-Ritz method and weak formulation of boundary value problems.
Discuss convergence criteria and completeness requirements in finite element discretization.

quiz.question: What characteristic defines isoparametric finite elements?
options: They use identical shape functions for both geometry and field variables
They apply only to 1D truss structures
quiz.explanation: Isoparametric elements employ the same interpolation functions to map coordinates and field variables.

subjects.name: Advanced Design of Mechanical Systems
objectives: CO1: Master system design approaches, concurrent engineering, and integrated CAE/CAD/CAM environments.
CO2: Apply Design for Manufacture (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles.
CO3: Explore sustainable design, life cycle assessment, and Design for Environment (DFE).

syllabus.topics: System Design Approach: Objectives, constraints, integrated process design, managing costs. Integrated Environments: CAD/CAE/CAM integration, digital simulation of product performance.
Material Selection & Component Design: Working principles, manufacturing design guidelines, redesign for machinability, minimization of core requirements in castings.
Design for Manufacture & Assembly (DFM/DFA): Process capability, feature tolerances, geometric tolerances, assembly limits, DFA guidelines, reducing part count.
Design for Environment (DFE): Environmental objectives, lifecycle assessment (LCA), design for recyclability, energy efficiency, and sustainability standards.

notes.title: Design for Assembly (DFA)
notes.explanation: DFA principles minimize assembly costs by reducing total part counts and simplifying product insertion geometry.
definitions: Evaluating whether parts can be combined into single components during conceptual design phases.
notes.example: Redesigning multi-piece sheet metal enclosures into single snap-fit molded plastic components.
exam_points: Manual and robotic assembly costs drop significantly when symmetrical, self-locating parts are utilized.

questions: Explain Boothroyd-Dewhurst Design for Assembly (DFA) guidelines and part reduction strategies.
Discuss geometric tolerancing and process capability in Design for Manufacture.

quiz.question: What primary objective characterizes Design for Assembly (DFA) methodologies?
options: Minimizing assembly time and total component part count
quiz.explanation: DFA focuses on reducing assembly costs and labor by streamlining component counts and handling ease.

subjects.name: Research Methodology
objectives: CO1: Formulate valid research problems, objectives, and hypotheses in mechanical engineering.
CO2: Master literature review techniques, data collection, statistical analysis, and research ethics.
CO3: Prepare technical reports, research proposals, and patent applications.

syllabus.topics: Research Problem Formulation: Sources, characteristics of good research problems, errors in selection, scope and objectives, data collection, analysis, and interpretation.
Literature Studies & Ethics: Effective literature review approaches, citation analysis, plagiarism detection, research ethics.
Technical Writing & Proposals: Report writing, research paper structuring, developing research proposals, presentation and review committee assessment.
Intellectual Property Rights (IPR): Patents, designs, trademarks, copyrights. Patenting process, innovation, Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT), licensing, and technology transfer.

notes.title: Patent Rights & IPR
notes.explanation: IPR protects technological inventions, granting legal monopoly rights for commercial exploitation.
definitions: All information publicly available before a given patent application filing date.
notes.example: Conducting prior art patent searches on advanced manufacturing mechanisms prior to filing utility patents.
exam_points: Patents require non-obviousness, novelty, and clear industrial utility.

questions: Discuss criteria and characteristics of formulating valid mechanical engineering research problems.
Explain the patent granting procedure and Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) framework.

quiz.question: What term describes all publicly disclosed technical documentation prior to a patent filing date?
quiz.explanation: Prior art establishes baseline novelty benchmarks during patent examination procedures.

subjects.name: Tribology
objectives: CO1: Understand friction, wear mechanisms, and surface topography in mechanical contacts.
CO2: Master hydrodynamic, hydrostatic, and elastohydrodynamic lubrication theories.
CO3: Explore bearing design, tribological testing, and advanced lubricants.

syllabus.topics: Introduction to Tribology: Friction, laws of friction, theories of friction. Wear: Classification, adhesive, abrasive, corrosive, fatigue, and erosive wear mechanisms. Surface topography and measurement.
Lubrication Fundamentals: Viscosity, viscosity index, Petroff's equation, Reynolds equation for fluid film lubrication, hydrodynamic journal and thrust bearings.
Hydrostatic & Elastohydrodynamic Lubrication: Hydrostatic bearing design and load capacity. Elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHL), Hertzian contact stress theory, film thickness calculations.
Bearing Materials & Solid Lubricants: Bearing metals, white metals, bronzes, polymers, solid lubricants (graphite, MoS2), tribological testing methods.

notes.title: Reynolds Equation for Lubrication
notes.explanation: Reynolds equation governs hydrodynamic pressure generation within fluid films separating moving machine elements.
definitions: A lubrication regime where moving surfaces are completely separated by a pressurized fluid film.
notes.example: Calculating load-carrying capacity in high-speed turbine journal bearings.
exam_points: Reynolds equation accounts for lubricant viscosity, film thickness geometry, and relative surface velocities.

questions: Derive Reynolds equation for one-dimensional fluid film lubrication.
Discuss adhesive and abrasive wear mechanisms and surface mitigation strategies.

quiz.question: What differential equation governs pressure distribution in hydrodynamic lubrication films?
quiz.explanation: Reynolds equation models fluid film pressure generation in lubricated bearings.

subjects.name: Project & Seminar
objectives: CO1: Execute independent mechanical engineering research, prototyping, and experimental testing.
CO2: Synthesize literature surveys and propose innovative design or manufacturing solutions.
CO3: Deliver technical seminar presentations and defend research outcomes.

syllabus.topics: Problem identification, literature survey, formulation of project methodology, software modeling (CAD/CAE/CFD).
Experimental setup fabrication, testing, data collection, and performance analysis.
Seminar presentation, report drafting, technical documentation, and project defense.

notes.title: Project Methodology & Prototyping
notes.explanation: M.Tech projects integrate advanced engineering principles with practical experimentation and simulation.
definitions: Building working physical or digital models to test design feasibility and performance.
notes.example: Simulating thermal fluid performance of heat exchanger prototypes using CFD software.
exam_points: Rigorous validation against analytical models ensures robust project outcomes.

questions: Describe the methodology, experimental setup, and results of your M.Tech project.
Discuss limitations and future scope of your research investigation.

quiz.question: What activity tests functional feasibility by constructing preliminary working models?
quiz.explanation: Prototyping validates design assumptions through physical or digital modeling.

subjects.name: Master's Dissertation (Thesis)
objectives: CO1: Execute an extensive, original research investigation in mechanical engineering.
CO2: Publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals or conferences.
CO3: Defend master's thesis before expert academic boards.

syllabus.topics: Full-scale experimentation, advanced numerical modeling, empirical data collection.
Result analysis, comparative evaluation against benchmark literature, thesis manuscript preparation.
Final thesis submission, open defense, and viva voce examination.

notes.title: Thesis Defense & Scholarly Publication
notes.explanation: Master's dissertations represent culminating independent research contributions evaluated through rigorous peer review.
definitions: The evaluation of scientific research by experts in the same field before academic publication.
notes.example: Publishing dissertation findings in SCI-indexed mechanical engineering journals.
exam_points: Thesis defenses assess methodological rigor, originality, and clarity of defense.

questions: Present core contributions, experimental validations, and conclusions of your Master's thesis.
Discuss industrial applications arising from your dissertation research.

quiz.question: What evaluative process reviews academic research manuscripts prior to journal publication?
quiz.explanation: Peer review ensures scholarly validity and methodological rigor in academic literature.

M.Tech. ECE.full_name: Master of Technology in Electronics and Communication Engineering (M.Tech. ECE)

subjects.name: Advanced Communication Networks
objectives: CO1: Understand advanced concepts in communication networking and network architectures.
CO2: Design and develop protocols for high-speed packet-switched and IP networks.
CO3: Analyze Quality of Service (QoS), queue management, and traffic engineering mechanisms.

syllabus.topics: Overview of Internet: Concepts, challenges, history. ATM overview. TCP/IP congestion and flow control, throughput analysis of TCP congestion control, TCP for high bandwidth-delay networks, fairness issues.

Real-Time Communications over Internet: Adaptive applications, latency and throughput issues. Integrated Services Model (IntServ), resource reservation, RSVP. Linearly Bounded Arrival Processes (LBAP), leaky bucket algorithm.

Packet Scheduling Algorithms: Requirements, choices, guaranteed service connections (GPS, WFQ, rate proportional algorithms). Active Queue Management: RED, WRED, virtual clock, control-theoretic analysis.
IP Address Lookup & Packet Classification: Grid of tries, cross-producting, and controlled prefix expansion algorithms for flow identification.
Admission Control & Differentiated Services: Effective bandwidth concept, measurement-based admission control. Differentiated Services (DiffServ) architecture and framework.
IPv4, IPv6, IP tunneling, IP switching, and MPLS. Overview of IP over ATM. MPLS architecture, framework, protocols, and traffic engineering issues.

notes.title: Leaky Bucket Algorithm & Traffic Shaping
notes.explanation: The leaky bucket algorithm regulates packet transmission rates, smoothing out traffic bursts in high-speed networks.
definitions: A mechanism that controls the rate of data injection into a network to prevent congestion.
notes.example: Controlling bursty video streaming traffic using leaky bucket policing in ATM and IP networks.
exam_points: Linearly Bounded Arrival Processes (LBAP) characterize bursty traffic constrained by burst size and average rate.

questions: Explain the leaky bucket algorithm and its role in traffic characterization using LBAP.
Discuss Integrated Services (IntServ) architecture and RSVP protocol operations.

quiz.question: What traffic conditioning mechanism smooths out bursty data streams by outputting packets at a constant rate?
quiz.explanation: The leaky bucket algorithm controls transmission rates and enforces strict traffic shaping profiles.

subjects.name: Wireless and Mobile Communication
objectives: CO1: Design cellular communication systems applying frequency reuse, cell splitting, and handoff techniques.
CO2: Analyze propagation path loss, small-scale fading, and multipath channel parameters.
CO3: Evaluate multiple-access technologies (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA) and higher-generation cellular standards (GSM, LTE, 5G).

syllabus.topics: Cellular Fundamentals: Design, frequency reuse, cell splitting, handover, co-channel interference reduction, channel assignment. GSM architecture, subsystems, logical channels, encryption, mobility management, call flows. 2.5G/2.75G standards (HSCSD, GPRS, EDGE).
Spectral Efficiency & Multiple Access: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA spectral efficiency comparisons, signal separation, wireless link budget, and power spectrum calculations.

Mobile Radio Propagation: Large-scale path loss, free-space model, ground reflection (two-ray) model, diffraction, scattering. Small-scale fading, impulse response, Doppler spread, flat and frequency-selective fading.
Equalization & Diversity: Receiver equalizers, adaptive equalization algorithms, diversity techniques (space, polarization, frequency), interleaving.
Code Division Multiple Access: IS-95 architecture, air interface, physical/logical channels, forward/reverse link operation, soft handoff, evolution to CDMA2000.
Higher Generation Standards: 3G evolved EDGE, 4G LTE architecture, protocols, call flow, VoLTE, UMTS, and introduction to 5G.

notes.title: Two-Ray Ground Reflection Model
notes.explanation: The two-ray ground reflection propagation model accounts for both direct line-of-sight and ground-reflected paths in mobile radio channels.
definitions: A radio propagation model predicting path loss proportional to $d^4$ at large distances.
notes.example: Calculating received signal strength for cellular base stations over flat terrain.
exam_points: Received power drops off much faster ($1/d^4$) with distance in the two-ray model compared to free-space ($1/d^2$).

questions: Derive the received power equation for the two-ray ground reflection mobile propagation model.
Discuss small-scale fading types classified by Doppler spread and time delay spread.

quiz.question: How does path loss scale with distance $d$ at large separations in the two-ray ground reflection model?
quiz.explanation: The two-ray model predicts received power falling off inversely with the fourth power of distance at large ranges.

subjects.name: Research Methodology and IPR
objectives: CO1: Formulate valid research problems, literature reviews, and research methodologies.
CO2: Master technical writing, research proposal drafting, and ethical publication standards.
CO3: Understand Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), patenting processes, and technology transfer.

syllabus.topics: Meaning of research problem, sources, characteristics of good research problems, errors in selection, scope and objectives, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and instrumentation.
Effective literature studies approaches, analysis of plagiarism, and research ethics.
Effective technical writing, report writing, research paper development, research proposal formatting, and review committee assessment.
Nature of Intellectual Property: Patents, designs, trademarks, copyright. Patenting process, innovation, Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).
Patent Rights: Scope, licensing, technology transfer, patent databases, geographical indications, and software IPR.

notes.title: Patents & Intellectual Property Rights
notes.explanation: IPR frameworks protect novel engineering inventions, software algorithms, and technological designs.
definitions: An exclusive legal right granted for an invention providing commercial monopoly for a limited duration.
notes.example: Filing utility patents for novel wireless communication transceiver architectures.
exam_points: Patents require novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability.

questions: Explain the criteria for patentability and the procedure for patent filing under PCT.
Discuss ethical guidelines in academic research and methods to avoid plagiarism.

quiz.question: What core legal requirement mandates that a patented invention must not be previously known in public domains?
quiz.explanation: Novelty ensures that an invention has not been previously disclosed publicly anywhere in the world.

subjects.name: Advanced Digital Signal Processing
objectives: CO1: Master discrete random processes, estimation theory, and linear signal models.
CO2: Apply optimum linear filters (Wiener and Kalman filters) for noise reduction.
CO3: Explore multirate digital signal processing, filter banks, and spectral estimation.

syllabus.topics: Discrete Random Processes: Ensemble averages, stationarity, autocorrelation, power spectral density, spectral factorization, Wold decomposition theorem.
Linear Signal Models: All-pole (AR), all-zero (MA), pole-zero (ARMA) models, Yule-Walker equations, Levinson-Durbin recursion.
Optimum Linear Filters: FIR Wiener filters, orthogonality principle, linear prediction, forward and backward linear prediction, Kalman filter recursive estimation.
Multirate Digital Signal Processing: Decimation, interpolation, sampling rate conversion by rational factors, polyphase filter bank structures, multistage implementation.

notes.title: Wiener Filtering & Orthogonality Principle
notes.explanation: Wiener filters compute optimum linear estimates of stationary random signals in the presence of additive noise.
definitions: The error signal in an optimum linear filter is orthogonal to all data used to estimate the desired signal.
notes.example: Removing channel noise from transmitted communication signals using adaptive Wiener filters.
exam_points: The Wiener-Hopf equations define the optimum filter tap weights minimizing mean square error.

questions: State and prove the orthogonality principle for optimum linear Wiener filters.
Derive the Wiener-Hopf equations for discrete-time FIR Wiener filter design.

quiz.question: What principle states that the estimation error in an optimum linear filter is orthogonal to the observation data?
quiz.explanation: The orthogonality principle ensures minimum mean square error by making estimation error orthogonal to input data.

subjects.name: Dissertation-I & Industry Training
objectives: CO1: Undertake original research and literature review in electronics and communication engineering domains.
CO2: Formulate research problems, design hardware/software architectures, and implement prototypes.
CO3: Prepare technical dissertation reports and defend research findings.

syllabus.topics: Literature survey, problem identification, feasibility assessment, research objective formulation, and methodology design.
Summer Industry Training (6-8 weeks) in reputed electronics industries or research laboratories.
Implementation, initial experimentation, progress evaluation, dissertation report drafting, and seminar presentation.

notes.title: Research Methodology & Problem Formulation
notes.explanation: Rigorous literature reviews identify research gaps, establishing novel contributions in ECE domains.
definitions: An unexplored question or missing perspective identified in existing scholarly literature.
notes.example: Formulating novel beamforming algorithms for 5G massive MIMO communication arrays.
exam_points: Clear problem statements and reproducible experimental evaluations are essential for successful M.Tech dissertations.

questions: Describe the research methodology, literature review findings, and proposed architecture for your dissertation.
Discuss evaluation metrics and experimental benchmarks used in your research study.

quiz.question: What document summarizes initial research progress, literature surveys, and problem formulations for M.Tech evaluation?
quiz.explanation: Dissertation-I documents literature surveys, problem formulation, and preliminary implementation progress.

subjects.name: Dissertation-II (Thesis)
objectives: CO1: Execute complete research investigations, hardware/software implementation, and empirical evaluations.
CO2: Analyze experimental results against state-of-the-art benchmarks and draw scientific conclusions.
CO3: Author peer-reviewed research papers and defend thesis findings before expert panels.

syllabus.topics: Full-scale implementation, algorithm tuning, hardware prototyping, and experimental performance evaluation.
Comparative analysis, ablation studies, result validation, and preparation of research manuscripts for publication.
Final thesis writing, formatting according to university guidelines, open defense, and viva voce examination.

notes.title: Empirical Evaluation & Thesis Defense
notes.explanation: Rigorous experimentation and peer-reviewed validation substantiate scientific contributions in Master's theses.
definitions: An experiment removing feature components to evaluate their individual contributions to system performance.
notes.example: Benchmarking proposed wireless transmission bit error rates against baseline modulation schemes.
exam_points: Thesis defense evaluations assess research originality, technical rigor, and clarity of presentation.

questions: Present the experimental results, performance comparisons, and conclusions derived from your thesis research.
Discuss potential future work and practical industrial applications arising from your study.

quiz.question: What experimental analysis removes individual system components to measure their specific impact?
quiz.explanation: Ablation studies systematically remove components to isolate their contribution to system efficacy.
